Meta Connect 2026 live: Updates from Mark Zuckerberg's keynote on AI glasses, VR and more
More smart glasses and possibly a VR headset are expected today
Meta Connect used to be all about VR, but in recent years, the event has come to be the launchpad for all of the company's hardware, Metaverse and AI projects. This year, we're expecting CEO Mark Zuckerberg to unveil a slew of new products across its smart glasses, headsets and AI portfolios. In fact, its own website for Connect says that the next two days will showcase "our latest breakthroughs in AI technologies, AI glasses and VR — designed to help you connect, create and do more of what you care about most."
Zuckerberg is slated to present the keynote speech at 7PM ET (4PM PT) later today, with additional developer talks and sessions scheduled for tomorrow. Our senior reporter Karissa Bell will be on the ground in Menlo Park, CA, reporting live from the company's headquarters. She'll be joined by myself and Devindra Hardawar in covering the news from the keynote live.
As a reminder, the company already unveiled a new series of Meta Glasses earlier this year, but is expected to show off a pair today that doesn't have cameras onboard. It's also been awhile since we've seen a Quest XR/VR headset from Meta, and it's quite likely that we'll learn more about a new model today. And in case you're getting deja vu, you might be remembering that another company had just launched a new pair of smart glasses last week. But Zuckerberg and co. most likely will have far more than one product and some weird demos to show off today.
It'll be a few more hours until Meta kicks off, and our liveblog will begin slightly before that. While you wait, we welcome
We're Live! New posts will appear automatically.
- 
    Meta doesn't have much additional info on the Charm just yet, and here's all it has to say on the Connect blog: "Muse Charm is a delightful and fun device built for you to talk and interact with your Muse. It brings the power of Muse with a state of the art real-time voice model into a device that fits in your pocket. We'll have more to share later this year."
- 
    Well I certainly wasn't expecting to see Muse Charm but I definitely like it a lot. It feels like a Tamagotchi met an AI wearable. For better or worse?
- 
    Get some rest, Karissa! And thanks for joining us everyone!
- 
    
- 
    And we're out. Be sure to check out all of our coverage on Meta's news tonight. I went long on the VR Glasses, they really do feel like the Vision Pro successor Apple gave up on.
- 
    And with that, the keynote has ended. That was a very packed hour.
- 
    
- 
    Muse Charm will be invading your privacy soon, folks!
- 
    Oh, we're getting a "one more thing." It's a little puck that looks about the size of an Apple Watch. It's for talking to your Muse agent. Zuckerberg says it's not finalized yet, but we are planning to have it ship "in time for the holidays" in December. They're calling it Muse Charm.
- 
    Oh great, you trap your Muse in a tiny keychain-sized device.
- 
    So... Very funny that Zuck hasn't mentioned the Meta VR Glasses also require a separate wired computing puck.
- 
    
- 
    The gasp I just gasped at Mahjong tiles appearing.
- 
    Zuck's pitch for the Meta VR Glasses evokes the original Jobs pitch for the iPhone. It's cinema, a computer and a console. $1,299!
- 
    Meta VR Glasses will ship this spring for $1299.
- 
    The Hologram Calling feature looks a lot more mature than the Vision Pro's Personas, that's for sure.
- 
    Meta is adding full-body photorealistic VR holograms. Boz jokes that Meta has finally solved the problem of legs in VR. Holograms are also coming to Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses.
- 
    A new Immersive Cinema mode in the Disney+ app will have immersive versions of Infinity War and Star Wars Ep. 4: A New Hope. It looks like live sports is going to be a major feature, too.
- 
    The VR glasses will also support the whole back catalog of Quest titles (if you opt for controllers – the glasses are compatible with Quest controllers) and Xbox Cloud Gaming.
- 
    The entire Quest library is supported with VR controllers, and you'll be able to play Xbox cloud streaming titles too.
- 
    
- 
    Boz is about to play a new version of Beat Saber in the VR glasses, he says he's playing on "medium" mode. It's one of 75 titles that will be ready when the glasses ship. "VR gaming is alive and well," Boz says.
- 
    Boz gave his Muse agent several tasks, and it looks like it heard all of his requests. Now he's playing a new version of Beat Saber made for hand support.
- 
    
- 
    Boz is watching an immersive National Geographic video shot in 3D. It appears to be just 180-degrees, like Apple's Immersive Video format. I'm seeing lots of cues from the Vision Pro here.
- 
    "Cinema. Computer. Console," A screen behind Zuck reads.
- 
    Zuck says that Meta executives have gotten to over 100 wpm on the Meta VR Glasses virtual keyboard. I tried that keyboard briefly and I definitely struggled, but maybe I need more practice (I probably need more practice).
- 
    Zuck claims Meta's CTO has reached 100 words per minute with the VR Glasses' virtual keyboard.
- 
    
- 
    Meta VR Glasses have Muse directly integrated into the operating system. The glasses also use hand and eye tracking, ie: no controller necessary.
- 
    We see images of a virtual keyboard on a table top. Cameron says he's inspired by them.
- 
    Palmer Luckey cameo in this VR Glasses video is .. interesting!
- 
    We're watching James Cameron, Palmer Lucky and other folks being wowed by these glasses.
- 
    
- 
    The VR glasses are the result of more than a decade of work, Zuck says.
- 
    He says it's about the weight of a deck of cards, I feel like there's more hardware coming...
- 
    There they are: Meta VR Glasses. A big cheer in the room from the section I assume is mostly Meta employees. They weigh about 100 grams and are "much lighter than Vision Pro," Zuck says.
- 
    He really shouted that.
- 
    Ha, that's the first metaverse mention of today, he says the company decided to focus less on it unless there was a breakthrough. "This is a breakthrough," he says.
- 
    Zuckerberg says "there in one more pair of glasses I want to show you."
- 
    You too can own a hilariously thick framed pair of glasses for nearly $1,000!
- 
    Meta is "finally catching up with demand" for its Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses and will be selling them in more countries, Zuck says.
- 
    
- 
    We're also getting a new celebrity collab for Meta Glasses with the "Lisa" frames. These are a new style of frame and case and each one comes with a charm inspired by her pets.
- 
    (Which one is Kylie.)
- 
    And the Meta Glasses in Adventurer are getting a price cut, starting at $249. That's a pretty good deal considering Gen 3 Ray-Ban Meta starts at $449.
- 
    Let's take a moment and consider how weird it is a tech keynote is going deep into classes eyeglass styling.
- 
    That sound you hear is hackers salivating at the opportunity to capture real-time video and audio from whoever they want.
- 
    
- 
    Dolby Atmos spatial audio capture from glasses sounds wild.
- 
    Meta is also updating its regular Ray-Ban Meta line with Gen 3. The Wayfarers are slimmed down, and there are new styles, including aviators. Gen 3 also supports Dolby Atmos for recording audio.
- 
    Personally, I'm far more interested in audio only glasses, just for listening to podcasts and audiobooks all day.
- 
    Wow, the essence of style.
- 
    Meta also had to redesign the internal electronic components for one of the new styles, the Clubmaster frames. These glasses are way thinner than other Ray-Ban Meta frames.
- 
    
- 
    Now we're moving onto audio glasses. "Without cameras, this opens up a lot of new design possibilities," Zuck says. They also have the longest battery of any of Meta's glasses.
- 
    Ah, Meta taking the annoying car maker approach to software features.
- 
    Hearing Enhancement will be coming first to Meta Glasses and will come to other glasses (Ray-Ban Meta, etc.) soon. It costs an additional $149 one-time payment to enable.
- 
    
- 
    I'm wary of these devices touting health features, as they're often a way to sanitize the bigger issues with them. I'm sure this Hearing Enhancement feature will be very useful to some people, though.
- 
    I got a chance to try a demo of this feature yesterday (with thick foam earplugs to simulate hearing loss) and it seemed to work very well during my brief time.
- 
    Last year, Meta showed off something called Conversation Focus to help people hear in noisy situations. This year, we're getting a feature called Hearing Enhancement, which is an FDA-cleared hearing aid replacement feature that is meant specifically for people with hearing loss or who are hard of hearing.
- 
    
- 
    All of these privacy features feel like table stakes for AI wearables.
- 
    Zuckerberg is talking through privacy, he mentions the recording light and Meta's attempts to address tampering. Meta is also working on private processing for glasses, which will add additional security to certain features.
- 
    This became the Nina Marie Daniele show, all of a sudden.
- 
    This video is giving us a sense of how Muse on Glasses can help with goals and provide more personalized guidance. In this case, it's a custom training plan with real-time feedback.
- 
    Agrippa sounds a bit too aggro, TBH.
- 
    Those Muse voices sound better than I'd expect, but I wonder how many people will start just talking to their devices like this.
- 
    Zuckerberg says that Meta is upgrading the built-in AI on its glasses so you can change it to be your Muses's voice and name (that also means we will finally have an alternative to "Hey Meta").
- 
    
- 
    You'll be able to change the sound of your Muse's voice, including accents, speed and even things like "sound like a cowboy." We just got another video of cute Muse avatars but I think Meta is really trying to hammer the point that this is a "personal" AI.
- 
    Zuck is giving his agent a very complex list of tasks and it said "working on sending you options now," I guess we'll find out later how much of that it caught.
- 
    Of course Zuck just can't stop making references to ancient Rome.
- 
    
- 
    Zuck is talking to his Muse which, of course, appears to be Roman? It's wearing a toga and name Agrippa.
- 
    We're going to get a live demo of Muse's new voice mode on Meta's AI glasses, this should be interesting.
- 
    Zuckerberg is giving us his pitch for AI glasses, why the company is betting so big on the form factor. He says the company has also "shifted" its focus to make its devices ready for AI superintelligence.
- 
    
- 
    On a personal note, my 7-year-old daughter just started wearing glasses for the first time. She loves them! But I'm worried about what happens when smart glasses for teens and kids becomes a thing.
- 
    Zuckerberg is back and we're onto the glasses portion of this keynote. It's like the price is right in here, a giant display of glasses opened up behind Zuck.
- 
    Wang says that there's going to be a new model out of Meta Superintelligence Lab "soon" but it's just a tease for now.
- 
    I am not looking forward to all of my older relatives who will start playing around with Muse, just because it looks cute.
- 
    
- 
    I wonder how much Meta wants to make the AI equivalent of an agentic WeChat for the rest of the world.
- 
    There's also some new shopping partnerships coming via Shopify and PayPaL. There are also a bunch of retailers that will work with Muse, as well as Instacart. This emphasis on shopping and retail makes a lot of sense when you think of what Zuck just said about Muse's business model depending on people actually buying stuff with their agent.
- 
    Oh, Muse can now buy anything on the internet via Shopify? I cannot imagine how that can go wrong. We're also seeing stores like Walmart and Best Buy integrate with it as well.
- 
    
- 
    Onto updates: Muse will be able to control your computer (a handy addition to the Mac app) and it's getting its own email address, which could be useful if you don't want to give it the keys to your email.
- 
    The news that Muse is available on computers gets one sad "Woo" from the crowd.
- 
    Wang claims real people have been using Muse to get reduced insurance rates, apparently it knocked someone's internet bill down by $85.
- 
    Wang is now doing his best to explain why people might want to use Muse. He says it's saving people real money, "it's a banger," he says.
- 
    Definitely not the Alexander Wang I was expecting. I'm out of the AI loop.
- 
    The cute robots will destroy us all, Karissa.
- 
    I will say that Meta was smart to make Muse avatars cute. Wang's is modeled after his own dog.
- 
    Can an AI agent get Alexandr Wang a comb?
- 
    
- 
    Alexandr Wang, Meta's Chief AI Officer, is now onstage. I can't remember the last time Zuckerberg ceded the Connect stage so quickly after entering. It says a lot about how important Muse/AI is to the company right now.
- 
    How long have these people actually been using Muse?
- 
    Zuckerberg says that Meta expects Meta will make money with Muse over time by taking a small cut of transactions handled by Muse and in the meantime they are giving people a large number of tokens for free to use Muse.
- 
    
- 
    I missed the news cycle around Muse's launch, when I saw people talking about this thing it felt like a fever dream. Give your AI agent a cute face, and you won't mind when it completely screws up a reservation, I guess.
- 
    Meta believing in people? Oh we're going to fact check that. Did they believe in teenage health with Instagram? With the sensitivity of misinformation during the last few presidential campaigns? Ugh.
- 
    Zuck is now giving the rundown on Muse, with a cute little animated Muse avatar smiling behind him. (Fun fact, you can change what your's looks like, mine is a cat.)
- 
    "I am more and more convinced that the reason why Meta exists ... is because we actually believe in people. Building is an act of love," Zuckerberg says. That's one I haven't heard from him before.
- 
    "The highest point of superintelligence is creation and invention, not just automation." We sure about that?
- 
    Zuckerberg is going right into hyping out Meta's AI agents. He is sounding a little like Evan Spiegel last week saying that people "have a lot of views" about what the future will look like. He is not giving his pitch about how AI will empower everyone and belongs to everyone not just "the few."
- 
    And we're right into personal superintelligence. "The future is for everyone," reads the screen behind Zuck.
- 
    
- 
    And what looks like a VR avatar of Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth appeared briefly before Zuckerberg walked out, notice his tee?
- 
    Whoa, tons of virtual windows, and that was a very realistic video chat avatar.
- 
    And light have come down and we're opening with a video, of course. It says "live demo" and appars to be a VR workstation.
- 
    The counter has been reset! Suspense.
- 
    1 minute to go! I'm sure Zuck has fully engaged his Human Mode.
- 
    Get comfy, I think the next hour will be very packed.
- 
    And because I just posted that, a countdown has now appeared. About 4 minutes to go!
- 
    Good evening folks! I'll be nerding out on potential VR news alongside Karissa. I have a feeling Valve is really going to regret launching the Steam Frame so close to this event.
- 
    We're just under 10 minutes to go until the keynote is supposed to start. The room has definitely filled up, but there are still plenty of people hanging out close to the stage taking photos and selfies. I wonder if we'll start on time.
- 
    It's common knowledge that Meta Glasses make up a huge chunk of the smart glasses market, but it's also still a leader in VR. While estimates vary on the exact figure, Meta is said to have over 50 percent marketshare in the VR headset market, with its Quest line of headsets has outselling every alternative for many years. Despite (or perhaps because of) its dominant position, we haven't seen new VR hardware from the company in almost two years.
- 
    I'm in! I have a seat towards the front of the press section, though people are very much still filing in.
- 
    Hello hello! I am just outside the keynote stage waiting for them to open the doors so we can get our seats. As usual, it's very hot in Menlo Park today so I'm happy to be in air conditioning.
- 
    While smart glasses and VR headsets are still far from common or mainstream, they're no longer something I'd consider the public to be unaware or ignorant of. And as commenter Caylpso points out below, the increased development could lead to these devices finding more useful places in our lives. Caylpso: "I enjoyed Meta's as the most comfortable bluetooth headset for meetings that I've ever worn. An audio-only pair of glasses with better battery life would be exactly what I want."
- 
    These last two years, we've seen an uptick in smart glasses launching. Samsung showed off its Galaxy XR headset at an October event in 2025, for instance, while Google has been talking up its Android XR platform for months. Before that, even, companies like Xreal, RayNeo, Even Realities and more have been hard at work developing heads up displays. While many of these have been around for a long time, this recent flurry of development has felt like a reaction to the positive reception to the Apple Vision Pro.
- 
    We are now just over an hour away from the keynote and it's just about dinner time here on the East coast. Before we devote our attention to Meta's upcoming announcements, it's worth looking at what the current state of the VR, XR and smart glasses market is like.
- 
    For all those who are eager to see what Meta might unveil today, we already have quite a good idea of what to expect. From a new "Project Phoenix" headset to smart glasses without cameras, it looks like facewear is definitely on the agenda.
- 
    I was going to take a break from the comments section and tell you all what we sort of think is going to be unveiled today, but there have been some good new ones! User "Display" said "Meta Display glasses 2! Lighter, thinner, and much better battery life! I don't even care if they don't have a 2nd display yet – obviously that would be sweet, but, I didnt have any eye strain issues, so, make them light and look like the non-displays! And to all the people calling them creepy – Easy. Make the punishment MUCH harsher for people who creep with them. For those of us who use our glasses as a POV camera for memories, don't punish US because there are creeps... Punish the crap out of the creeps so they're less-inclined to creep." I wonder if there has been enough time for Meta to make new Display glasses. And i do think people are calling this category of devices, not specifically Meta's Display alone, creepy. I think Apple also caught a lot of flak for its Audio Intelligence features two weeks ago.
- 
    Meanwhile, user "Jorge Gottheil" in the comments below said "I think it would be amazing if the programming of the glasses was possible as open source, for my use case I would need very high definition (like 4k) and fast connection to a MacBook Pro (sports application) or a newer iPhone and run a model with a database against what I am seeing in realtime, with a color HUD...are we anywhere close to that?" I'll leave it to our VR expert Devindra Hardawar to weigh in shortly, but I have yet to hear about anything like that that isn't a heavy-duty desktop-tied VR headset like the ol' Vive. And that feels a little like outdated information from me.
- 
    We're about two and a half hours from Zuckerberg delivering his presentation. It appears there are quite a few VR fans genuinely curious what might be unveiled today. For instance, commenter "DirkDiggler" said below: "I hope they allow a USB-C displayport connection between your PC and the headset. That would be epic and make the PCVR community grow and grow and grow and grow." and another reader DookieJawz has helpfully replied that the feature has been available on the quest for a while, and is available for download via Meta's desktop client.
- 
    I'm actually shocked there are already quite a few comments below! Extremely generic user "Your Username" said "New stuff being announced is great. But, if it's anything like last year, it ends up being a dud. The Display glasses were never released outside the USA, even though they were promised for early 2026. Let's hope they learned something there." Well I think we're anticipating quite a lot more devices today.
- 
    If you're wondering what Meta might have up its sleeve today, it's safe to say that AI and VR are on the agenda. I am old (?) enough to recall when Meta Connect used to be about the Oculus headsets and... one odd year, the "metaverse." Have we adopted that term yet?
- 
    Hello everyone! Welcome to our liveblog of Meta Connect 2026. It's been a busy few weeks, and we're clearly in the thick of tech launch season. But are people excited for more AI and VR? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.title: DIA Diamond Jewelry nâng tầm trải nghiệm kim hoàn với mô hình boutique
articles.text:
Thị trường hàng xa xỉ đang chứng kiến sự chuyển biến rõ nét trong hành vi tiêu dùng. Sản phẩm vẫn là trung tâm, song chất lượng dịch vụ, khả năng cá nhân hóa cùng trải nghiệm thực tế tại cửa hàng đang tác động trực tiếp đến quyết định chi tiêu.
Báo cáo năm 2025 của Bluebell Group khảo sát 1.500 người tiêu dùng có thu nhập cao tại châu Á cho thấy nhóm khách hàng này tiếp cận hàng xa xỉ thận trọng hơn, ưu tiên giá trị dài hạn. Bên cạnh chất lượng chế tác, trải nghiệm tại điểm bán đóng vai trò then chốt trong việc xây dựng sự gắn kết và lòng trung thành.
Sự thay đổi này thể hiện rõ trong ngành kim hoàn. Khách hàng vẫn tìm hiểu nguồn gốc, thông số kỹ thuật hay chứng thư giám định. Nhưng họ cũng muốn biết vì sao thiết kế đó phù hợp với cá tính, đáp ứng hoàn cảnh sử dụng và mang dấu ấn gì sau khi rời cửa hàng.
Điểm bán không chỉ là nơi giao dịch
Với các món đồ giá trị cao, cửa hàng vật lý giữ vai trò khó thay thế. Đây là nơi người mua quan sát độ lửa viên đá, ướm thử tỷ lệ lên tay và lắng nghe tư vấn chuyên môn trước khi đưa ra quyết định.
Dù vậy, chức năng của showroom đang được định nghĩa lại. Thay vì xếp kín sản phẩm lên kệ kính, một số thương hiệu chuyển sang mô hình boutique với danh mục tuyển chọn, kiến trúc giàu dụng ý và quy trình tư vấn mang tính cá nhân hóa.
Tại đây, chuyên viên tư vấn không chỉ báo giá hay thông số kỹ thuật. Họ đồng hành cùng khách hàng phân tích sự khác biệt giữa các lựa chọn, cân bằng giữa thẩm mỹ, công năng và ngân sách.
Điều này đặc biệt cần thiết khi thị trường đồng thời hiện diện cả kim cương tự nhiên lẫn kim cương nuôi cấy (LAB-grown diamond). Hai dòng đá sở hữu nguồn gốc, định mức chi phí và giá trị đầu tư khác biệt. Việc cung cấp thông tin minh bạch giúp khách hàng đưa ra quyết định phù hợp nhất với bản thân.
DIA thử nghiệm mô hình boutique experience
Nắm bắt xu hướng này, DIA Diamond Jewelry là một trong những đơn vị tiên phong ứng dụng mô hình boutique experience trong phân khúc trang sức kim cương tại Việt Nam.
Không gói gọn trong các dòng nhẫn cưới hay cầu hôn truyền thống, DIA mở rộng dải sản phẩm phục vụ nhiều cột mốc cá nhân: một đợt thăng tiến, sinh nhật tuổi 30, khởi đầu công việc mới hay mục tiêu tài chính vừa hoàn thành.
Tại showroom mới trên phố Xã Đàn (Hà Nội), khu vực trưng bày được thiết kế theo cảm hứng gallery nghệ thuật. Thay vì phân loại sản phẩm đơn thuần theo kích thước hay mức giá, cách bài trí định hướng sự chú ý của khách hàng vào câu chuyện, tính ứng dụng và độ tinh xảo của thiết kế.
Đáng chú ý, DIA giới thiệu cả kim cương tự nhiên và kim cương LAB. Thương hiệu không đặt hai dòng sản phẩm vào thế so sánh hơn - kém, mà căn cứ vào nhu cầu và ngân sách của từng cá nhân. Người đề cao tính độc bản, giá trị vĩnh cửu có thể lựa chọn kim cương tự nhiên; trong khi khách hàng yêu thích viên chủ lớn, thiết kế thời thượng với mức giá dễ tiếp cận có thêm lựa chọn từ kim cương LAB.
Đưa câu chuyện khách hàng vào không gian bán lẻ
Điểm nhấn khác biệt tại không gian DIA Xã Đàn là khu vực "Wall of Moment" - nơi lưu giữ những dấu mốc đáng nhớ cùng khách hàng.
Trải nghiệm mua sắm không kết thúc sau bước thanh toán. "Wall of Moment" giúp ghi lại lý do phía sau mỗi món trang sức: một lời cầu hôn, kỷ niệm ngày cưới, dấu ấn mua căn nhà đầu tiên hay đơn giản là món quà người phụ nữ tự thưởng cho chính mình. Cách tiếp cận này chuyển trọng tâm từ lời kể của thương hiệu sang ý nghĩa thực tế của sản phẩm đối với chủ nhân.
Bên cạnh đó, dịch vụ cá nhân hóa hộp đựng trang sức bằng charm cho phép khách hàng trực tiếp tham gia hoàn thiện món đồ. Từ khâu chọn giác cắt kim cương, kiểu chấu giữ viên chủ cho đến chi tiết trang trí hộp, mỗi sản phẩm đều mang đậm dấu ấn cá nhân.
Không gian boutique còn mở ra cơ hội kết nối cộng đồng. Trong dịp khai trương vừa qua, showroom Xã Đàn trở thành điểm hẹn để khách hàng trực tiếp thử trang sức, tương tác và chia sẻ cảm nhận.
(Nguồn: DIA Diamond Jewelry)

articles.title: Qualcomm chính thức ra mắt Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6: Lần đầu tiên, chip mang tên “Elite” không còn là mạnh nhất
articles.text:
Chúng ta đã quen với việc mỗi thế hệ Snapdragon 8 Elite đại diện cho chip di động mạnh nhất của Qualcomm. Tuy nhiên, đến Gen 6, hãng lại mang đến một bất ngờ chưa từng có.
Qualcomm vừa trình làng hai bộ xử lý cao cấp mới gồm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 và Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. Việc bổ sung phiên bản Extreme đồng nghĩa mẫu Elite thông thường, dù có cấu hình thuộc hàng mạnh nhất thị trường, không còn giữ vị trí cao nhất trong dòng chip di động của hãng.
Cả hai đều được sản xuất trên tiến trình 2 nm và sử dụng kiến trúc CPU Oryon do Qualcomm tự phát triển. Tuy nhiên, phiên bản Extreme được ưu tiên hàng loạt công nghệ về đồ họa, AI và quay video, hướng tới những mẫu smartphone đắt tiền nhất.
Cùng đạt 5 GHz, vậy điều gì khiến bản Extreme khác biệt?
Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 và Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 đều sử dụng cụm CPU gồm hai nhân Prime đạt xung nhịp tối đa 5 GHz cùng sáu nhân Performance chạy ở mức tối đa 4 GHz. Hệ thống được hỗ trợ bởi 16 MB bộ nhớ đệm Oryon Flex Cache.
Qualcomm tuyên bố đây là những bộ xử lý di động đầu tiên vượt qua cột mốc 5 GHz. Riêng phiên bản Extreme được quảng cáo có hiệu năng CPU cao hơn 13% nhưng tiêu thụ ít năng lượng hơn 37% so với Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5.
Điều đáng chú ý là Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 tiêu chuẩn vẫn có chung tiến trình, kiến trúc CPU và xung nhịp tối đa 5 GHz. Đây dự kiến cũng là bộ xử lý xuất hiện phổ biến hơn trên các mẫu smartphone cao cấp của nhiều nhà sản xuất.
Khác biệt lớn bắt đầu xuất hiện ở phần đồ họa. GPU Adreno trên phiên bản Extreme được tích hợp các nhân ma trận AI chuyên dụng, có thể xử lý tác vụ học máy song song với quá trình dựng hình truyền thống.
Các nhân này được sử dụng cho Adreno Neural Fusion, công nghệ của Qualcomm nhằm nâng độ phân giải và tạo thêm khung hình bằng AI. Hãng tuyên bố hệ thống có thể duy trì tốc độ khung hình cao, hạn chế hiện tượng nhòe hoặc lỗi hình ảnh, đồng thời giảm tới 40% điện năng cần thiết cho quá trình dựng hình.
GPU trên bản Extreme được công bố có hiệu năng cao hơn 44% và hiệu suất năng lượng tốt hơn 40% so với thế hệ trước. Con chip còn sở hữu 18 MB bộ nhớ Adreno High-Performance Memory riêng, một trang bị không xuất hiện trên Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 tiêu chuẩn.
Qualcomm đã hợp tác để tích hợp nền tảng đồ họa mới vào Unreal Engine, Unity và Messiah Engine của NetEase. Những công nghệ như Lumen Global Illumination, MegaLights và Nanite Virtualized Geometry cũng được hỗ trợ. Một số trò chơi dự kiến tận dụng nền tảng này gồm Honkai: Star Rail, Monster Hunter Outlanders và Neverness to Everness.
“Extreme” còn thể hiện ở AI và khả năng quay video
Hexagon NPU thế hệ mới được Qualcomm công bố có hiệu năng tăng 35%, trong khi hiệu suất trên mỗi watt cải thiện 33%. NPU này bổ sung Element Accelerator, cơ chế suy luận micro-tile và lượng bộ nhớ chia sẻ lớn hơn 50% so với thế hệ trước.
Cả hai bộ xử lý đều có thể thực hiện những tác vụ AI agent ngay trên thiết bị. Tuy nhiên, Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 sở hữu dung lượng bộ nhớ chia sẻ dành cho NPU lớn hơn 50%, cho phép chạy trực tiếp các mô hình Mixture of Experts có hơn 30 tỷ tham số và cửa sổ ngữ cảnh lên tới 32K.
Qualcomm cũng nâng cấp Sensing Hub với hai NPU siêu nhỏ và hai bộ xử lý hình ảnh luôn hoạt động. Theo hãng, sức mạnh tính toán của thành phần này tăng 85%, trong khi hiệu suất năng lượng được cải thiện 20%.
Một ứng dụng đáng chú ý là Personal Scribe. Công cụ này có thể xử lý tin nhắn, email và các cuộc trò chuyện để tạo thành một kho kiến thức cá nhân ngay trên thiết bị, thay vì phải liên tục gửi dữ liệu lên máy chủ đám mây.
Khả năng chụp ảnh được đảm nhiệm bởi hệ thống ba ISP Spectra AI 20-bit. Qualcomm cho biết hệ thống mới có thể xử lý lượng dữ liệu AI trên từng điểm ảnh chi tiết gấp 256 lần trước đây.moto
Phiên bản Extreme tiếp tục tạo khoảng cách bằng khả năng quay video 8K ở tốc độ 60 khung hình/giây và quay chậm 4K 240 khung hình/giây. Con chip còn hỗ trợ phần cứng cho codec Advanced Professional Video, công cụ màu Elite Color Engine với LUT 3D thời gian thực và giải mã VVC/H.266. Trong đó, quay 8K 60 FPS, 4K 240 FPS và ghi hình APV là những tính năng dành riêng cho bản Extreme.
Bộ đôi chip mới sử dụng modem Snapdragon X105 5G, được chuẩn bị cho tiêu chuẩn 3GPP Release 19. Tốc độ tải xuống lý thuyết đạt 14,8 Gbps, tải lên 4,2 Gbps, đồng thời hỗ trợ liên lạc vệ tinh cho tin nhắn, thoại, dữ liệu và video.
Hệ thống FastConnect 8800 cung cấp tốc độ mạng nội bộ tối đa 11,6 Gbps, hỗ trợ cấu hình Wi-Fi 4x4 và được chuẩn bị sẵn cho Wi-Fi 8. Bluetooth 6.0, UWB và Thread cũng nằm trong danh sách kết nối.
Như vậy, chữ “Extreme” không đơn thuần là cách Qualcomm đặt tên cho một phiên bản có xung nhịp cao hơn. Hai con chip cùng đạt 5 GHz, nhưng bản Extreme được mở khóa thêm về đồ họa AI, bộ nhớ chuyên dụng, khả năng chạy mô hình lớn và quay video chuyên nghiệp.
Những smartphone đầu tiên sử dụng chip Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6
Motorola Signature 27 được giới thiệu là smartphone đầu tiên chính thức hỗ trợ Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. Xiaomi cũng dự kiến trang bị con chip này cho Xiaomi 18 Pro Max, trong khi Xiaomi 18 Pro sử dụng Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 thông thường.
Cách phân chia này phần nào cho thấy vị trí mà Qualcomm dành cho hai bộ xử lý. Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 sẽ xuất hiện trên phần lớn smartphone cao cấp, còn phiên bản Extreme hướng tới những thiết bị muốn đẩy xa hơn khả năng chơi game, AI và đặc biệt là quay phim.
Lần đầu tiên, smartphone Android dùng chip Qualcomm có thể hỗ trợ quay video 8K ở tốc độ 60 khung hình/giây hoặc quay chậm 4K 240 khung hình/giây. Phiên bản Extreme còn xử lý trực tiếp codec Advanced Professional Video, cho phép người dùng quay và chỉnh sửa video chuyên nghiệp ngay trên điện thoại.
Bên cạnh Hexagon NPU, hai bộ xử lý Gen 6 còn tích hợp Sensing Hub với hai NPU siêu nhỏ. Thành phần này có thể học từ tin nhắn, email và các cuộc trò chuyện để xây dựng kho kiến thức cá nhân, phục vụ những trợ lý AI có khả năng ghi nhớ thói quen của người dùng.
Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 không hề mất đi vị thế của một chip flagship. Tuy nhiên, với sự xuất hiện của phiên bản Extreme, cái tên “Elite” đứng riêng đã không còn đại diện cho cấu hình mạnh nhất mà Qualcomm có thể đưa lên smartphone.
Tuấn Lê

articles.title: Never use ChatGPT for these five tasks - Engadget
articles.text:
Never use ChatGPT for these five tasks
It's not a lawyer, it's not a doctor and it's definitely not your therapist.
The roster of people who have self-pwned by typing the wrong information into ChatGPT continues to grow. Samsung engineers, the acting director of America's cyber defense agency, self-represented litigants who provide citations to court cases that don't exist, a man who swapped table salt for sodium bromide after asking how to cut salt from his diet... the list is too long.
Even everyone's favorite all-lowercase techbro CEO Sam Altman concedes that what you're sharing with ChatGPT isn't privileged. Speaking to podcaster Theo Von in July 2025, he highlighted how courts could force OpenAI to hand over chats, calling it "very screwed up."
Tell a doctor, lawyer or therapist something and the law shields that conversation, but telling ChatGPT creates an audit trail. There's a non-zero risk here, given that ChatGPT chats have been subpoenaed, exposed by a share button, indexed by Google and preserved by a court order post-deletion — all in the last 18 months.
Sure, the chatbot is arguably a useful tool for research (check that case citations are real), coding (even the bugs ship), explaining concepts (there's no correlation between confidence and accuracy) and drafting (delete the prompt from your email before hitting send). But the areas below are where more than 900 million weekly users could create problems for themselves.
So to that end, don't use ChatGPT (or any other AI chatbot)...
1. For legal advice
Law and data science researcher Damien Charlotin maintains a public database that, to date, has logged more than 2,000 court decisions worldwide hamstrung by ChatGPT. These are cases where a judge has caught AI-fabricated citations, quotes or arguments in a filing.
It's not just self-representing litigants here. While they top the list with 1,175 records at the time of writing, lawyers come second with 815 records. It seems judges are growing tired of these shenanigans, with courts more recently imposing large fines well into the thousands-of-dollars range in a growing number of matters. Although the US makes up the largest number of cases in this data, judges in the UK, South Africa, Israel, Australia and Spain have all caught the same behavior. Where a tool was identified in those cases, ChatGPT was named more than any other.
OpenAI addressed this issue last October when it updated ChatGPT's usage policies. Those policies now prohibit using its services for "tailored advice that requires a license" unless a licensed professional is involved. Beyond false citations, ChatGPT chats have no legal privilege, so anything typed into it about a live dispute is fair game for the other side's lawyers in discovery. Go ahead and ask general questions like what a tort is (great if you need help falling asleep), but save the detailed questions about your own dispute for an actual lawyer.
2. As a therapist or counselor
OpenAI estimated last year that 0.15 percent of ChatGPT's weekly active users have conversations that include explicit indicators of potential suicide planning. That unfortunately works out to more than a million people per week, with hundreds of thousands more users exhibiting signs of psychosis or mania. Altman has said young people in particular treat ChatGPT as a therapist or life coach and, again, that nothing shields these chats.
The parents of 16-year-old Adam Raine sued OpenAI for wrongful death in August 2025, alleging that ChatGPT reinforced their son's suicidal ideation before his death. Since then, OpenAI has reworked its crisis responses with input from more than 170 clinicians. The company has also added parental controls to ChatGPT, though child safety experts are skeptical of ChatGPT for Teens, the age-gated version launched alongside those changes.
Researchers have found that chatbots tend to reinforce a user's existing beliefs through sycophantic responses, in some cases feeding delusional thinking rather than challenging it. Describe an argument with your spouse, for example, and the model will work from your account's context alone, probably serving you an affirming verdict back regardless. Legislators are beginning to wake up to this, with states including Illinois, Nevada and Maine having passed laws prohibiting AI from delivering therapy or making therapeutic decisions.
3. With confidential work information
It should go without saying that uploading confidential work documents to a third-party chatbot is always a bad idea. Unfortunately, too many people don't seem to realize this.
Ironically, Madhu Gottumukkala, the former acting director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, didn't. He uploaded at least four contracting documents marked "for official use only" to the public version of ChatGPT last summer, triggering security alerts and a Department of Homeland Security review. Even more ironically, the tool had been blocked for most other DHS employees at the time; Gottumukkala requested a special exception to use it. Senator Chuck Grassley followed up in February this year demanding an account of what was exposed, but predictably, nobody was really held to account. Gottumukkala was eventually shuffled elsewhere within the DHS.
Samsung banned gen AI tools on company devices back in May 2023 after engineers notably pasted internal source code into ChatGPT. Accompanying that ban was an internal memo reasoning that data sent to such platforms lives on external servers where it's difficult to retrieve or delete, and could end up disclosed to other users. On consumer accounts, chats can also be used to train new models unless you've chosen to opt out. But opted-out data is still stored and breachable, and subject to legal process. Pasting client data or anything subject to employer controls or NDAs into a personal ChatGPT discussion is almost always going to be a fireable offense; Samsung's memo threatened exactly that.
4. To seek medical advice
The same October 2025 policy update that bans users from using ChatGPT as a lawyer also restricted people from seeking medical advice via the chatbot. HIPAA binds doctors, insurers and their business partners, but not OpenAI. Thus, health data that's legally shielded in a patient portal or between a doctor and patient has no such protection if it's disclosed to ChatGPT.
Researchers from Northeastern University reported in July that while OpenAI has tightened ChatGPT's handling of suicide and self-harm, those safeguards largely don't extend to other conditions. Their work found that conversations involving conditions like eating disorders, insomnia, substance abuse and bipolar disorder didn't trigger the safeguards, and that hiding intent made every tested model's protections more likely to fail.
In a particularly wacky case of ChatGPT medical advice gone bad, a 60-year-old man spent three weeks in the hospital last year after asking the chatbot how to cut chloride from his diet. He ended up convinced that sodium bromide, a toxic substance with a long half-life, was a safe swap for table salt. He bought it online, took it for three months and wound up in an emergency department convinced his neighbor had poisoned him. While the clinicians in this man's case never saw his chat logs, ChatGPT offered bromide as a chloride substitution when they gave the same question to the bot themselves.
5. To do anything involving passwords, ID numbers or account details
Fast Company found nearly 4,500 shared ChatGPT conversations lurking in Google search results last July. These included exchanges describing addiction, abuse and mental health struggles in enough detail to potentially identify their authors. The chats wound up indexed because people checked a "make this chat discoverable" checkbox in the share menu which, apparently, happened without them understanding what it did. OpenAI was quick to respond, killing the feature within a day of the report and purging conversations from Google.
As part of The New York Times' copyright lawsuit, OpenAI was ordered in May 2025 to retain every consumer chat log, deleted and temporary conversations included. That obligation ran until September 26, 2025, and logs preserved during that window remained accessible to the plaintiffs. A judge later terminated that order, meaning OpenAI no longer has to preserve all its ChatGPT data. But for four months, it did, and it could happen again.
It's vital to be aware that ChatGPT remembers what you tell it by default. That significantly raises the stakes for sensitive matters like passwords and account details, since they can persist across sessions and resurface in later conversations if mentioned even once. Passwords, one-time login codes, Social Security and passport numbers, full card or bank account details and photos of ID documents should never go into a prompt. Every one of those puts you at danger of identity theft if a chat is breached or otherwise accessed.
Altman has called for an "AI privilege" (of course he has) to fix these confidentiality issues. But until lawmakers create one, the safe assumption is that anything typed into ChatGPT could someday be read back to you by someone else. If you aren't comfortable with that, don't put it into a prompt.

articles.title: The old cybersecurity model is breaking | TechCrunch
articles.text:
As concern over AI safety and rogue agents continue to make headlines, it’s no surprise that cybersecurity stocks are rising, or that investors are pouring massive amounts of capital into startups trying to build the next generation of security for an AI-native world. We’re even seeing companies like Instinct and Simile bring in nine-figure checks and valuations that wouldn’t have made sense a few years ago.
With a front row seat to it all is Shardul Shah, a partner at Index Ventures who’s spent nearly two decades investing in cybersecurity and enterprise software — including six consecutive rounds in cloud security startup Wiz, which Google acquired for $32 billion earlier this year in one of its largest acquisitions ever.
On this episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Shah joins Rebecca Bellan to break down why he thinks periodic, human-in-the-loop security can’t keep up anymore, and why Index continues investing in AI-native security companies at stages that once required much more proof.
Subscribe to Equity on YouTube, Apple Podcasts, Overcast, Spotify and all the casts. You also can follow Equity on X and Threads, at @EquityPod.

articles.title: Anthropic ra mắt Claude Opus 5.5: Mạnh ngang Fable 5.1 nhưng giá rẻ hơn nhiều
articles.text:
Mô hình mới vượt Fable 5.1 ở nhiều bài kiểm tra lập trình, trong khi giá API chưa bằng một nửa và người dùng gói trả phí được nới giới hạn sử dụng.
Ngày 22/9, Anthropic ra mắt Claude Opus 5.5 và gọi đây là mô hình mạnh nhất hãng từng thử nghiệm. Opus 5.5 đã có mặt trên ứng dụng Claude bản web và di động, qua API với mã claude-opus-5-5, cũng như trên Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud và Microsoft Azure.
Điểm lạ nằm ở vị trí của Opus 5.5 trong dòng sản phẩm. Theo Anthropic, mô hình mới làm được hầu hết công việc ở mức ngang Claude Fable 5.1, mô hình cao cấp nhất dành cho người dùng phổ thông mà hãng vừa ra mắt đầu tháng 9. Trong khi đó, chi phí vận hành của Opus 5.5 thấp hơn Opus 5 khoảng 40% với các tác vụ thông thường, và tốc độ tạo phản hồi nhanh hơn Opus 5 trên 30%.
Giá API chưa bằng một nửa Fable 5.1
Opus 5.5 có giá 4 USD (khoảng 105.000 đồng) cho mỗi một triệu token đầu vào và 20 USD (khoảng 524.000 đồng) cho mỗi một triệu token đầu ra. Opus 5 trước đó có giá lần lượt 5 USD và 25 USD. Token là đơn vị nhỏ mà mô hình dùng để đọc và viết văn bản, nên đây là con số chính quyết định hóa đơn của doanh nghiệp và lập trình viên.
Với Fable 5.1, mức giá là 10 USD (khoảng 262.000 đồng) cho đầu vào và 50 USD (khoảng 1,31 triệu đồng) cho đầu ra. Theo VentureBeat, giá token cơ bản của Opus 5.5 rẻ hơn Fable 5.1 khoảng 60%.
Bộ nhớ đệm (tính năng giúp mô hình không phải xử lý lại phần nội dung lặp đi lặp lại) cũng giảm giá. Mỗi một triệu token đọc từ bộ nhớ đệm có giá 0,2 USD (khoảng 5.200 đồng), giảm 60% so với Opus 5. Người cần phản hồi nhanh hơn có thể chọn chế độ Fast với giá gấp đôi, 8 USD đầu vào và 40 USD đầu ra (khoảng 210.000 và 1,05 triệu đồng).
Vượt Fable 5.1 ở mảng lập trình
Anthropic công bố Opus 5.5 đạt 66,4% trên Terminal-Bench 4.0, bài kiểm tra khả năng tự thao tác dòng lệnh để hoàn thành công việc. Fable 5.1 đạt 55,8%, Opus 5 đạt 52,3%. Trên CursorBench 4.0, Opus 5.5 đạt 57,8% so với 51,8% của Fable 5.1. Ở FrontierCode v1.1, khoảng cách hẹp hơn, 54,4% so với 50,3%.
Với công việc văn phòng, mô hình mới đạt 1.846 điểm Elo trên GDPval-AA v2.1, cao hơn Fable 5.1 (1.735) và Opus 5 (1.708). Ở các bài kiểm tra khả năng điều khiển máy tính như OSWorld 2.0 hay đọc biểu đồ Chartography, cách biệt chỉ còn khoảng một điểm phần trăm.
Anthropic cũng đưa ra vài ví dụ từ thử nghiệm nội bộ. Trong một tác vụ chuyển mã nguồn từ ngôn ngữ C sang Rust, Opus 5.5 hoàn thành sau 9,5 giờ với chi phí thấp hơn 51%, trong khi Fable 5.1 mất 12 giờ. Một tác vụ rà soát mã nguồn khác, Opus 5 cần hơn 20 giờ, Opus 5.5 làm xong trong chưa tới 3 giờ.
So với đối thủ, OfficeChai tổng hợp rằng Opus 5.5 dẫn trước GPT-6 Astra của OpenAI ở phần lớn bài kiểm tra, như Terminal-Bench 4.0 (66,4% so với 57,9%) hay Humanity's Last Exam khi được dùng công cụ (67,7% so với 57,2%). GPT-6 Astra vẫn thắng ở AutomationBench, bài kiểm tra tự động hóa quy trình doanh nghiệp, và Terminal-Bench-Science (64,6% so với 58,7%).
Chính Anthropic cũng lưu ý rằng ở mức này, chênh lệch điểm benchmark không còn phản ánh chính xác năng lực, và khoảng cách thực tế giữa Opus 5.5 với Fable 5.1 "hẹp hơn những gì điểm số cho thấy".
Code gọn hơn, nhưng lỗi trên mỗi dòng tăng
Một đánh giá độc lập của Sonar, công ty chuyên về chất lượng mã nguồn, cho thấy bức tranh nhiều chiều hơn. Trên 544 tác vụ lập trình có kiểm thử, Opus 5.5 đạt tỷ lệ vượt qua 87,68%, gần như ngang Opus 5 (88,6%). Mô hình mới viết ít hơn 27,5% số dòng code và dùng ít hơn 40% token đầu ra, tổng số vấn đề phát hiện giảm 42%.
Tuy vậy, mật độ lỗi lại tăng 12%, lên 644 lỗi trên mỗi triệu dòng code. Nhóm lỗi xử lý đồng thời (khi nhiều luồng chạy song song và tranh nhau tài nguyên, loại lỗi khó tái hiện và khó sửa) tăng 44%, trở thành nhóm lỗi lớn nhất. Ở chiều ngược lại, lỗ hổng bảo mật mức nghiêm trọng nhất giảm 53%. Nói cách khác, Opus 5.5 viết ít và gọn hơn, nhưng lập trình viên vẫn cần kiểm tra kỹ, nhất là với code chạy đa luồng.
Yêu cầu nhạy cảm có thể bị chuyển sang mô hình cũ
Vì năng lực trong lĩnh vực sinh học và an ninh mạng ngang Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5 dùng bộ cơ chế bảo vệ tương tự. Một số yêu cầu về an ninh mạng sẽ được chuyển sang xử lý bằng Opus 4.8. The New Stack cảnh báo việc này có thể khiến các hệ thống AI tự động nhiều bước nhận kết quả từ những mô hình có năng lực khác nhau mà không hay biết. Các nhà nghiên cứu bảo mật và khoa học sự sống đủ điều kiện có thể đăng ký chương trình xác minh riêng để được nới hạn chế.
Với lập trình viên, Opus 5.5 kèm vài thay đổi phải sửa code. Chế độ suy luận (thinking) luôn bật và không thể tắt. Việc ép mô hình gọi một công cụ cụ thể có thể báo lỗi. Những ứng dụng hiển thị đoạn văn bản giữa các lần gọi công cụ làm thông báo tiến độ cũng cần điều chỉnh.
Người dùng trả phí được nới giới hạn
Cùng với Opus 5.5, Anthropic nâng giới hạn sử dụng theo chu kỳ 5 giờ cho các gói Pro, Max, Team và Enterprise tính theo số người dùng. Người đăng ký cũng được tặng một lượt đặt lại giới hạn, dùng được bất kỳ lúc nào đến hết ngày 22/10.
Anthropic cho biết Claude Sonnet 5.5 và Haiku 5.5 sẽ ra mắt trong vài tuần tới.

articles.title: Thực thi chiến lược hiệu quả
articles.text:
Trước đây hay cho rằng, chiến lược thất bại là do thực thi. Nay, để chiến lược được thực thi hiệu quả thì đầu tiên chiến lược phải đúng: đúng về xác định mục tiêu, về tạo nguồn lực cho thực thi, về cách thức thực thi, về cán bộ cho thực thi. Chiến lược phải chọn đúng trận đánh, có vũ khí đặc biệt, cách đánh độc đáo và có tướng giỏi. Nếu thực thi không hiệu quả thì đầu tiên phải xem lại chiến lược. Thí dụ, chiến lược đặt ra mục tiêu bẩy trái đất mà trong chiến lược lại không chỉ ra điểm tựa ở đâu thì thực thi sẽ không thể hiệu quả.
Chiến lược và thực thi có phải 2 việc, 2 người không? Trước đây, chiến lược và thực thi là 2 việc khác nhau, là 2 giai đoạn tách biệt. Nay, chiến lược là thực thi và thực thi là chiến lược. Chiến lược hình thành trong thực thi, và thực thi liên tục điều chỉnh chiến lược. Chiến lược và thực thi là 1. Chiến lược và thực thi là 1 vòng lặp liên tục. Người xây dựng chiến lược phải là người chịu trách nhiệm thực thi.
Vậy vai trò của HĐQT và CEO trong xây dựng và thực thi chiến lược thế nào? Mô hình trước đây: HĐQT làm chiến lược, CEO thực thi. Nay, HĐQT giữ phương hướng, CEO sở hữu chiến lược và kết quả. HĐQT là người đặt câu hỏi chiến lược và quyết định các lựa chọn chiến lược. CEO là người biến các lựa chọn đó thành chiến lược sống và kết quả thực tế. HĐQT quyết định: đi ngành nào, đầu tư bao nhiêu, chấp nhận rủi ro đến đâu. CEO quyết định: cạnh tranh bằng cách nào, tổ chức ra sao, dùng người nào, xác định các thứ tự ưu tiên và điều chỉnh.
Thực thi hiệu quả có phải là điều hành hàng ngày không? Trước đây, thường chú trọng vào việc điều hành hàng ngày của CEO. Nay, CEO phải tập trung xác định đúng việc, đúng người, đúng tổ chức, đúng nhịp, đúng kết quả. Thực thi chiến lược của CEO không phải là làm nhiều việc hơn, mà là làm ít việc hơn, làm đúng vài việc quan trọng, bởi đúng người, với đúng nhịp điều hành, cho đến khi tạo ra kết quả. Cụ thể như sau:
1- Về đúng việc: Biến chiến lược thành 3-5 ưu tiên cụ thể, mọi nguồn lực, ngân sách và lãnh đạo đều tập trung vào những ưu tiên đó.
2- Về đúng người: Chiến lược phải có người sở hữu, có chủ, ở tất cả các cấp. Tức là có người lo nghĩ ngày đêm về chiến lược, chính sự lo nghĩ ngày đêm này mà ra cách làm đột phá giúp chiến lược thành công. CEO phải là người dẫn dắt trực tiếp. Thực thi chiến lược trước hết là vấn đề lãnh đạo, sau đó mới là vấn đề quản lý. Chiến lược phải có đội quản lý cấp trung cốt cán làm nòng cốt thực thi. Thiếu cái này là thiếu xương sống của tổ chức để thực thi chiến lược hiệu quả.
3- Về đúng tổ chức: Đồng bộ toàn bộ tổ chức theo chiến lược. Các bộ phận phải đồng hướng, thực hiện điều chỉnh để toàn bộ Cty đồng hướng theo chiến lược. Đây là việc CEO phải làm.
4- Về đúng nhịp: Thực thi theo chu kỳ ngắn, học nhanh, điều chỉnh nhanh. Làm -> Đo -> Học -> Điều chỉnh -> Làm tiếp. Người Việt Nam nếu thiếu nhịp điều hành tuần/tháng/quý thì rất khó hoàn thành các công việc dài hơi. Đây là sự khác biệt rất căn bản giữa phương Tây và phương Đông, quản lý phương tây ưu tiên nhiều hơn đến hệ thống, mà ít nói đến nhịp điều hành.
5- Về đúng KPI kết quả: Xác định đúng các kết quả cần đạt được (các outcome, chứ không phải output), và dùng KPI để đo các kết quả đó.
Nguyễn Mạnh Hùng, Nguyên Ủy viên Trung ương, Nguyên Bộ trưởng Bộ Khoa học và Công nghệ

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Ayoub says companies can fence AI in, like banks did
articles.text:
Companies cannot fully govern AI systems, but they can build a fixed fence around them, Google DeepMind’s Kareem Ayoub said. He pointed to banks in the late 1980s and early 1990s. They put trading algorithms inside fixed rules they could check.
Ayoub, DeepMind’s vice president of AI technical strategy, spoke to Bloomberg’s Tom Mackenzie on Wednesday at HumanX in Amsterdam. He said the safety debate comes down to a tension between exponential capability and linear governance.
“You may not be able to fully govern the system itself, but you can build a deterministic governance perimeter around it,” Ayoub said of the banks’ approach.
He split the problem into three parts. One is the role AI should play in research and development. Another is how transparent systems must be. The third is who controls them. Google’s Frontier Safety Framework, which sets capability thresholds and mitigations, is part of the answer, he said.
Mackenzie noted that Anthropic’s Dario Amodei wants to pace the frontier. Demis Hassabis has called for an industry-led regulator modelled on FINRA, the US brokerage watchdog, Mackenzie said. Ayoub said guardrails will need partnerships beyond tech companies.
Frontier AI, used for email
Ayoub described a gap between what the technology can do and how companies use it. At the frontier, it speeds up drug discovery, translates ancient texts and helps detect gravitational waves. Inside businesses, the focus often lands on drafting or summarising email, he said.
He said the shift from the model to the agent as the product began around the end of 2025. An agent wraps a model in memory, tools and internet access so it can work through long, multi-step tasks. The strongest returns so far are in software engineering, he said.
The best companies he works with share four habits, Ayoub said. They build safe sandboxes quickly instead of waiting for multi-year IT projects. They do not bet against model progress. They measure what they care about. And their leaders use the tools themselves.
“The best businesses ask: will what I’m building be ten times better if the underlying model is ten times better?” he said.
Companies fail when they reward staff for hiding their AI use, he said. They also fail when leaders use the tools only superficially. As the cost of intelligence falls, he hopes more spending goes to checking outputs rather than producing more of them.
The mood at DeepMind
Mackenzie closed by asking about morale. He cited researchers who have left this year and Hassabis’s move to chairman. Google shifted its AI leadership to Koray Kavukcuoglu in California in August.
Ayoub said he had little to add to what has been reported. He said AGI is Hassabis’s life mission. He recalled Hassabis saying at Google I/O that, looking back, we will probably realise we were in “the foothills of the singularity”. He also pointed to the energy around the Gemini programme, led by Kavukcuoglu.
DeepMind launched the DeepMind Institute this month to debate AGI. Former DeepMind researchers are also building their own companies, including world-model startup Emulate.
“The future is no longer a forecasting challenge. It becomes a design problem,” Ayoub said.

articles.title: Meta Connect 2026: The 7 biggest announcements
articles.text:
Meta announced a slate of new wearables during its annual Meta Connect showcase on Wednesday. The star of the event was the new Meta VR Glasses, which pack virtual reality tech into a lightweight smart glasses-style frame with a tethered puck. Meta also announced new pairs of screen-free smart glasses, along with some new AI features and style and frame options.
Meta Connect 2026: The 7 biggest announcements
This year’s Meta Connect featured a new lightweight VR wearable and camera-free Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses.
You can catch up on all the highlights from this year’s Meta Connect below.
Meta’s latest wearable offers full virtual reality in a smart glasses-style form factor. Unlike a typical VR headset, the VR Glasses don’t have any straps, and Meta says they’re “five times lighter than Meta Quest 3” at just 100g. Similar to Google’s Project Aura, the glasses are tethered to a pocket-sized puck with the compute hardware, battery, and storage, including a Qualcomm Snapdragon Reality Elite, 128GB of storage, and 12GB of RAM. The 5K micro OLED “Infinite Display” has 2412 x 2288 pixels per eye, with a refresh rate of up to 120Hz.
The Meta VR Glasses are launching in spring 2027 for $1,299, pricier than the Meta Ray-Ban Display but less expensive than the Apple Vision Pro, while offering similar features. Users can connect the glasses to a Mac or Windows laptop for use as a virtual external display, with an option for a virtual surface keyboard and touchpad.
The VR Glasses also have access to the full Meta Quest catalog of apps and games and support for Xbox Cloud Gaming. Meta says the glasses are “the first IMAX Enhanced certified VR device ever,” and users will be able to watch “immersive live sports” with them as well as 3D movies. They even have a “hologram” feature that creates a “photorealistic digital version of your face” for using in calls while wearing the glasses, reminiscent of the “personas” on the Apple Vision Pro.
Meta is launching camera-free smart glasses
The highlight of the Ray-Ban Meta Audio is the feature they don’t have: built-in cameras. You can use them for things like listening to music, taking calls, or chatting with an AI assistant, but they can’t take pictures or record video — features that have sparked privacy and harassment concerns around Meta’s other glasses.
Meta says the new audio-only glasses are also its “lightest, slimmest AI glasses yet,” weighing just 43g. They offer up to 12 hours of battery life per charge, or 48 hours with the charging case. The Ray-Ban Meta Audio will launch on October 13th starting at $349 with 23 different color and lens combinations.
Refreshed Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 arrive with battery and design upgrades
Meta launched an updated version of its main Ray-Ban Meta glasses, starting at $449. The Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 offer up to nine hours of battery life, one hour more than the Gen 2. They also have “a new customizable action button for instant access to Meta AI” and a new six-mic array that Meta says “cuts more than 90% of background noise.”
The Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 has a slimmer design than the Gen 2 as well, with 27 color and lens combinations, including new Zena and Aviator frame styles. Notably, one thing that hasn’t changed is the built-in LED light that indicates when the glasses are recording, which Meta rolled out a privacy fix for last month.
Budget glasses launch along with new glasses styles
Alongside its pricier Ray-Ban glasses, Meta also announced some updates to its in-house line of glasses. It’s launching a new lower-cost version of the Meta Adventurer, which will start at $249 for a basic design with black frames and gray lenses, launching October 23rd.
Meta is also introducing a new “Mix & Match” program for customizing its glasses with different frames, lenses, and case colors. Plus, its EssilorLuxottica collection is getting two new styles, Capri and Nova, and the Kylie Jenner Starfire frames are getting a new ivory colorway. Meta’s also launching a new collaboration collection with Lisa of Blackpink.
Meta Glasses are expanding to more countries starting today, too, including Singapore, South Korea, Mexico, and the United Arab Emirates, with availability in Brazil “coming soon.”
Meta Ray-Ban Display is coming to more regions with some new features
A year after they originally launched, the Meta Ray-Ban Display are coming to more regions. The glasses are on sale in the UK and Canada starting today, and they’ll be available in France, Italy, and Germany starting on October 13th. Meta’s also introducing online ordering for customers in those regions and the US.
Meta’s launching a new Explore app for Display glasses where users will be able to “browse and use a growing selection of experiences built for your glasses.” The Meta Ray-Ban Display is also getting photo editing, an improved calendar, and mirrored phone notifications. Plus, Meta says the “hologram” feature launching on its VR Glasses is rolling out on the Meta Ray-Ban Display “in Early Access on WhatsApp to Meta Ray-Ban Display users in the US later this fall.”
After launching its new Muse assistant earlier this month, Meta says it’s “working on” bringing the AI to its smart glasses. When it arrives on the glasses, Muse will be able to do things like guide your workouts, log meals, book appointments, and “help buy products you see.”
Meta also announced some new features for Muse, including video calls with a customizable live avatar of the AI. Plus, Muse agents are getting their own email addresses for completing tasks and communicating with users.
Meta is making an AI ‘charm’
Mark Zuckerberg teased one last device, Muse Charm, a small AI gadget that houses the Muse agent and looks a little bit like a supersized Tamagotchi. More details will be shared “soon,” he said, but the product is supposed to ship in time for the holiday season.

articles.title: Apple links landmarks on its Maps app to Hidden Histories podcast episodes - Engadget
articles.text:
Apple links landmarks on its Maps app to Hidden Histories podcast episodes
They’re part of the app's Guides feature and are available for select landmarks in five US cities.
Apple now links to Hidden Histories podcast episodes within Maps for select landmarks in five US cities. As Apple Insider has noticed, certain landmarks in San Francisco, Los Angeles, New York City, Chicago and Washington, DC now show a panel in Maps that links straight to podcasts about their histories when you view their information in the app.
When you tap the panel in Maps, it'll take you to an interface where you'll see the rest of the landmarks in the city with linked podcast guides. The New York ones, for instance, include talks on Times Square, the Statue of Liberty, Central Park, the Museum of Broadway, Grand Central Terminal, the Charging Bull, Studio 54 and Tin Pan Alley. The Los Angeles podcasts include episodes on the history of the Hollywood Sign and the Hollywood Walk of Fame, while San Francisco's include Alcatraz and the Farallon Islands.
The Hidden Histories podcasts live under the Guides section in the Maps app. Like other things under Guides, such as lists of places to go curated by various publishers, you can tap the + icon and add podcasts to your collection. You can then revisit and listen to them another day by pulling up the panel from the bottom part of Maps and then looking at the "Your Guides" section.

articles.title: Exclusive: Zoox grounds Atlanta test fleet after workers report toxic gas exposure symptoms
articles.text:
Zoox has grounded its autonomous vehicle test fleet in Atlanta after safety drivers were potentially exposed to carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, or hydrogen sulfide gas inside its vehicles last month, TechCrunch has learned. The repeated incidents led one worker to file a complaint with the Occupational Safety and Health Administration, which opened an inquiry and told Zoox to investigate the exposures.
As many as 40 workers were possibly exposed to the gases in the vehicles, according to a letter from OSHA to Zoox that TechCrunch viewed, though the Amazon-owned company says the number is lower.
Zoox put at least one group of workers back on the road in a different car after one vomited and the rest reported exposure symptoms, a contractor told TechCrunch. That second car may have also contained potentially toxic gases, he said, because the workers experienced another bout of exposure symptoms later that day.
“They made us go right back in the field after we said we were throwing up,” Jay Davis, one of the contractors who got sick in mid-August, told TechCrunch in an interview. “I emailed HR, told her what’s going on, and I told her I feel like it’s messed up that y’all made us go [back out].”
Workers reported exposure symptoms and strange smells through much of last month until August 22, when someone called 911 for a sick worker. The facility in northwest Atlanta has operated at limited capacity since then, with the test vehicles quarantined while Zoox investigated the exposures, according to two employees. Zoox’s purpose-built robotaxis, which are all electric, are not affected.
TechCrunch spoke to Davis, who filed the OSHA complaint, along with one current and two former employees for this story. The other three workers were granted anonymity to discuss private company matters and because they fear retaliation.
The illnesses come as Zoox branches into new cities and expands its existing operations in places like Las Vegas and San Francisco, in a bid to catch market leader Waymo. This rapid growth has put some safety monitors at risk. As TechCrunch previously reported, contractors have sustained injuries from sudden braking and swerving in the Zoox test vehicles. Waymo has also reported similar test driver injuries to OSHA.
Exactly what gases the Zoox employees were exposed to remains unclear. Davis said he and two other workers who became sick were told at the emergency room that their symptoms were consistent with carbon monoxide exposure. The complaint filed with OSHA mentions possible carbon dioxide, or CO2, exposure.
Zoox told OSHA in a September 10 letter, viewed by TechCrunch, that it examined its test vehicles for signs of CO2 and replaced their 12-volt batteries. Damaged batteries can produce hydrogen sulfide gas, which creates a “rotten egg” smell. Some of the employees who spoke to TechCrunch said they noticed a similar smell in the cars. (After this story was published, Zoox told TechCrunch it has detected no damage to the batteries and no signs of hydrogen sulfide gas.)
Zoox identified 28 employees who rode in six test vehicles that had an “unexplained odor,” the company said in its letter to OSHA. Zoox told OSHA that 10 workers “voluntarily underwent medical evaluation” to “determine whether any exposure had occurred.” Zoox said in the letter that it received only “one medical report identifying CO2 exposure.”
Zoox told TechCrunch it hasn’t identified the presence of carbon monoxide, which is odorless, in its vehicles. The company said it consulted an outside medical expert to help investigate the issues and that the only gas it detected in the impacted vehicles was CO2.
In the letter to OSHA, the company said it will add CO2 monitors to the vehicles, and Zoox told TechCrunch that these devices will be able to detect other gases like carbon monoxide and hydrogen sulfide. OSHA has since closed its inquiry.
“The safety and well-being of our Zoox test fleet operators is our primary concern in this situation,” the company told TechCrunch. “We are taking ongoing, appropriate, and cautious actions to investigate the reported events as necessary and support any needs from our operators. While we investigate these reports thoroughly, we have ceased operations of our test vehicles in this market.”
Known risks
Cars produce carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide when they burn fuel. These gases can enter a vehicle if there is a leak in the exhaust system; they can also build up if a vehicle runs inside an enclosed space for an extended period. It’s a common enough problem that the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration investigated Ford for six years over reports of carbon monoxide buildup in its Explorer SUVs.
In its letter to OSHA, Zoox said it tested the vehicles’ exhaust systems for leaks and performed a “smoke test” for cabin intrusions. It did not say whether it found any evidence of either. The company also removed all the 12-volt batteries, inspected them for damage, and replaced them. It did not tell OSHA whether it found evidence of damage to the batteries.
The company keeps its test vehicles running through much of a given day, in part to maintain sensor calibration and reduce the onboard self-driving computer’s boot time. Zoox uses an exhaust-capture system at its indoor depots — similar to what is used to capture truck fumes at firehouses — designed to mitigate the buildup of toxic gases.
Zoox modifies the Highlander SUVs it uses for its test fleet. Most of that work focuses on adding sensors and an autonomy computer. But the company makes other changes, too, including adding an interior “snorkel” above the central infotainment screen that pushes air toward rear-seat passengers, the employees told TechCrunch.
Zoox said it doesn’t modify the ventilation systems in these SUVs. But making any changes to a vehicle can increase the risk that gases will leak into the cabin. In the Ford investigation, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said in 2023 that the highest levels of carbon monoxide were found in police vehicles that had added sirens, lights, and other modifications, all of which can create sealing issues.
Zoox is an outlier among major robotaxi developers because its test fleet vehicles have internal combustion engines. Waymo, Tesla, Avride, and Motional all use electric vehicles, which don’t produce exhaust gases. May Mobility’s test fleet includes some hybrid vans, and Nvidia uses a small number of gas and electric Mercedes-Benz sedans.
“Everybody got quiet for some reason”
Davis and the other employees said individual safety monitors started reporting possible exposure symptoms to Zoox at the beginning of August.
The incidents Davis experienced on August 14 were more acute because four workers were riding in the SUVs together — a practice Zoox uses while training new employees.
Davis told TechCrunch the first signs of trouble appeared early that morning.
“Everything was fine. We was all laughing and talking, you know, just having a normal workday, and then everybody got quiet for some reason,” he said.
Davis recalled that one of his colleagues asked if anyone else in the SUV was “feeling weird.” The crew was approaching their scheduled morning break at 10 a.m., so the workers stopped at a Chick-fil-A. As soon as they got out of the car, Davis said one of his co-workers started throwing up. He and the others felt lightheaded.
They called the dispatcher at Zoox’s Atlanta depot, who arranged for the SUV to be towed back to base, he said. Meanwhile, Zoox arranged for an Uber to take the workers back to the depot.
“As soon as we get back to base, we’re thinking, okay, since we’ve been sick and said we was lightheaded, you know, we’re gonna have like, you know, mild duties for the day. Just sit down, you know, get yourself back together,” Davis said. “No, they put us in another [test car] and they told us to go back to work.”
After driving all afternoon, Davis said he and his colleagues went to a food court. He started vomiting after just a few bites of his meal.
Davis contacted a representative from HireArt, the third-party contractor that technically employs Zoox’s test drivers in Atlanta. He said the representative gave him a workers’ compensation hotline number and told him to call Poison Control. Three of the workers went to the emergency room, where they were evaluated for carbon monoxide exposure.
Davis said the emergency room doctor did not detect elevated carbon monoxide levels in his system. But he and others were told their symptoms were consistent with carbon monoxide poisoning.
Workers continued getting sick in the days that followed, according to all four workers who spoke to TechCrunch. On August 22, one contractor got sick enough that someone at the depot called 911.
It’s not immediately clear who called 911 or what happened to the sick worker. As for the four employees who reported symptoms on August 14, Zoox ordered them to take what it described as a random drug test in the days that followed.
This story has been updated with new information from Zoox.

articles.title: OpenAI's FDE chief says 80% of enterprise AI problems are deployment
articles.text:
Most companies that struggle with enterprise AI are not waiting for better models, OpenAI’s head of forward deployed engineering said on Wednesday. In about 80% of cases, Colin Jarvis said, the problem is deployment. Companies do not yet know how to roll AI out, govern it or prove they can trust it.
Glasgow-based Jarvis leads OpenAI’s forward deployed engineers (FDEs), who work inside customer companies to get its models into production. He spoke to Alex Hern of The Economist at HumanX in Amsterdam.
“I don’t personally feel a lot of pressure to race ahead on model development itself,” Jarvis said.
In the other 20% of cases, customers say the model cannot yet do the job, he said. Those gaps are now narrow and specialist, such as a task in semiconductor design, rather than everyday office work.
What FDEs do
The team started out as mostly software engineers, Jarvis said, because building on the raw API meant writing everything from scratch. With tools such as Codex, about 50% of each project is now custom work, down from about 90%. That has shifted hiring toward domain experts, including a former investment banker, former scientists and a chip verification engineer.
Every engagement starts with a two-day visit. The team asks business leaders to ignore AI and name the biggest levers in their business. It then works on whichever that turns out to be.
At one semiconductor company, engineers spent maybe 80% of their time on bugs from overnight jobs, Jarvis said. OpenAI built a system that finds the root cause, proposes a patch and applies it after an engineer reviews it. It spread from one department to the whole business. The company estimates it saves roughly $40m to $50m a year.
Other projects include an agent that iterates car part designs from plain-language instructions, for a European manufacturer. Another helps draft clinical trial documents, where a human always stays in charge.
Why pilots fail
Jarvis named two common mistakes. Companies pick a use case because it seems to fit AI, not because it matters. Or they get one good use case working in one department, and it stays a demo that never spreads.
The companies that succeed measure success by production use, not proofs of concept, he said. One semiconductor customer has about 35 use cases live after roughly 18 months. It built a central team to scale projects and placed small groups of engineers in each business unit.
FDEs have no financial incentive tied to usage, Jarvis said. They are measured on whether a project reaches production and moves a real metric. When OpenAI’s embeddings were too slow for a Klarna search service, he told the company to use an open-source model instead.
“From OpenAI’s side, we should always be temporary,” he said.
The pace question
Hern noted that Sam Altman was at the UN that day, as pressure grows to slow AI down. Jarvis said OpenAI has shown it will pause when it reaches the limits of its safety frameworks. He said he thought it paused its main reinforcement learning run “in September this year”.
OpenAI published its own post on the pause on 18 August. It describes a two-week pause in reinforcement learning training on its latest models. It also says its largest planned frontier run stayed on hold. Altman has since said OpenAI will set its own pace without waiting for Congress.
Jarvis said FDEs help test whether safety frameworks built in a lab hold up in messy real companies.
OpenAI is not alone in sending engineers into clients’ offices. AWS is spending $1bn on the same model, and Microsoft launched a $2.5bn deployment business in July.
