articles.title: Số phận gói thầu hơn 291 tỷ ở Nghệ An sau khi lãnh đạo y tế Việt Mỹ, Thứ trưởng Thuấn bị bắt
articles.text:
Trao đổi với PV VietNamNet, một lãnh đạo UBND tỉnh Nghệ An cho biết, địa phương cũng đang rà soát các gói thầu liên quan Công ty Việt Mỹ. Một số nội dung thuộc diện mật do liên quan quá trình kiểm tra, điều tra của cơ quan công an.
Theo lãnh đạo tỉnh, bệnh viện là chủ đầu tư nên phải chịu trách nhiệm chính trong tổ chức mua sắm, đấu thầu và thực hiện hợp đồng. Việc gia hạn hai gói thầu được thực hiện theo trình tự, thủ tục quy định.
Ông Nguyễn Viết Bình, Phó Giám đốc Bệnh viện Ung bướu Nghệ An cho biết, Sở Y tế đã chỉ đạo bệnh viện rà soát các gói thầu của Công ty Việt Mỹ, tuy nhiên hiện chưa có kết quả.
Gói thầu số 02 và số 03 thuộc Dự án Mua sắm thiết bị y tế chuyên dùng tại Bệnh viện Ung bướu Nghệ An được UBND tỉnh phê duyệt tháng 12/2024, với tổng mức đầu tư 305 tỷ đồng, gồm 150 tỷ đồng từ ngân sách tỉnh và 155 tỷ đồng từ Quỹ Phát triển hoạt động sự nghiệp của bệnh viện. Trong đó, gói thầu số 02 có giá trị hơn 291 tỷ đồng.
Dự án gồm hệ thống PET/CT, hệ thống Cyclotron, hệ thống CT Scanner 64-128 lát cắt/vòng quay và hệ thống áp lực dương; đồng thời cải tạo, nâng cấp khu vực sản xuất chất đồng vị phóng xạ F-18 FDG và khu vực lắp đặt hệ thống PET/CT, Cyclotron.
Ngày 20/3/2025, Giám đốc Bệnh viện Ung bướu Nghệ An phê duyệt kết quả lựa chọn nhà thầu gói thầu số 02 “Mua sắm thiết bị y tế chuyên dùng”. Liên danh Việt Mỹ - Thành An được lựa chọn thực hiện gói thầu với giá trị hơn 291 tỷ đồng.
Hợp đồng ban đầu có thời gian thực hiện 10 tháng. Do không hoàn thành theo tiến độ, gói thầu đã được gia hạn lần đầu. Đến ngày 9/6/2026, Bệnh viện Ung bướu Nghệ An tiếp tục có văn bản gửi Sở Tài chính đề nghị gia hạn thời gian thực hiện hợp đồng đối với gói thầu số 02 và số 03.
Ngày 18/6, Sở Tài chính có văn bản gửi Chủ tịch UBND tỉnh về việc gia hạn hai gói thầu. Theo báo cáo của Sở Tài chính, với gói thầu số 02, nhà thầu gặp khó khăn trong sản xuất, vận chuyển thiết bị do thiếu nguyên liệu trên toàn cầu và ảnh hưởng của chiến tranh. Việc di chuyển của các nhóm kỹ sư nước ngoài sang Việt Nam để lắp đặt, căn chỉnh và đào tạo cũng bị ảnh hưởng.
Đối với gói thầu số 03, trong quá trình thi công phát sinh một số công việc theo yêu cầu của đơn vị cung cấp thiết bị và đơn vị sử dụng nhằm bảo đảm điều kiện lắp đặt, vận hành hệ thống. Một số phần việc chỉ có thể hoàn thiện sau khi hệ thống thiết bị được lắp đặt.
Ngày 25/6/2026, UBND tỉnh Nghệ An thống nhất cho phép gia hạn thời gian thực hiện hợp đồng đối với gói thầu số 02 và số 03 đến ngày 30/9/2026.
Bệnh viện Ung bướu Nghệ An được yêu cầu nghiêm túc rút kinh nghiệm, chấn chỉnh công tác quản lý thực hiện các hợp đồng phải gia hạn nhiều lần.
Một tháng sau, ngày 25/7/2026, Cơ quan CSĐT Bộ Công an khởi tố vụ án xảy ra tại Công ty CP Đầu tư Y tế Việt Mỹ và các đơn vị liên quan về các tội “Buôn lậu, Vi phạm quy định về kế toán gây hậu quả nghiêm trọng”.
Quá trình điều tra mở rộng, cơ quan công an tiếp tục khởi tố một số bị can, trong đó có ông Trần Văn Thuấn, Thứ trưởng Bộ Y tế, về tội “Nhận hối lộ”. Ông Lê Đình Thanh Sơn, Giám đốc Bệnh viện Đa khoa tỉnh Phú Thọ và ông Nguyễn Huy Ngọc, Phó Chủ tịch UBND tỉnh Phú Thọ, cũng bị khởi tố về cùng tội danh trong quá trình mở rộng điều tra.
Tại Bệnh viện Ung bướu Nghệ An, đến giữa tháng 9, gói thầu số 02 vẫn chưa hoàn tất. Một số thiết bị đã được lắp đặt nhưng chưa hoàn thiện đồng bộ để đưa vào vận hành; hệ thống Cyclotron và một số hạng mục liên quan đang được hoàn thiện.
Theo báo cáo của đơn vị cung cấp thiết bị, hệ thống Cyclotron dự kiến đến ngày 27/9/2026 hoàn thành việc lắp đặt và hướng dẫn vận hành, sát thời hạn hợp đồng được gia hạn đến ngày 30/9.
Lãnh đạo tỉnh Nghệ An cho biết, gói thầu số 02 đã được gia hạn lần thứ hai. Nguyên nhân chậm tiến độ là Công ty Việt Mỹ chưa cung cấp đầy đủ thiết bị. Đến nay, dù gần đến ngày hết thời gian thực hiện theo tiến độ được gia hạn, gói thầu vẫn chưa hoàn thành, thiết bị chưa được cung cấp đầy đủ và chưa đồng bộ để đưa vào vận hành.
Về phương án xử lý khi thời gian gia hạn lần thứ hai kết thúc, lãnh đạo UBND tỉnh Nghệ An cho biết các cơ quan chức năng sẽ tiếp tục rà soát, xem xét trên cơ sở quy định pháp luật và tình hình thực hiện hợp đồng. Nếu nhà thầu không hoàn thành đúng tiến độ, cơ quan có thẩm quyền sẽ xem xét xử lý vi phạm hợp đồng và áp dụng các biện pháp theo quy định của pháp luật về đấu thầu.

articles.title: Dario Amodei asks UN Security Council to back a ban on AI bioweapons
articles.text:
Dario Amodei is asking the UN Security Council to start with narrow agreements on AI, such as a ban on using it to make biological weapons.
Speaking to the Council via video link today, the Anthropic chief executive calls AI the most important global security issue.
Amodei is the third briefer at the meeting in New York, convened by France. According to the Security Council Report, it is the Council’s first meeting focused specifically on the safety risks of increasingly capable AI.
“Four years ago, it could barely write a line of code or solve a high school math problem. Today, it writes most of the code at Anthropic,” Amodei says.
If that trajectory holds for one or two years, maybe less, AI will reach what he has called a country of geniuses in a data center.
Earlier today, Anthropic announced that Claude had discovered a new enzyme system with CRISPR-like features, a finding he describes as preliminary.
Amodei sees two main risks: misuse, for example by bioterrorists building biological weapons, and models advancing beyond their developers’ ability to control them.
Both, he says, are serious enough for the Council rather than only for economic or technology ministries.
“If managed poorly, I even believe that AI could be a risk to humanity as a whole,” he says.
He says Anthropic tests every model for dangerous capabilities in areas such as cybersecurity and biology, and publishes its risk reports.
The company has also reported four cases this summer in which its Claude models reached real third-party systems during tests.
“We will slow down as much as necessary in order to make sure that every successive AI technology that we release is actually safe,” Amodei says.
He repeats his 12 September call to pace AI progress. It includes external evaluators inside labs with employee-like access, which he compares to a food inspector, along with industry and government cooperation on standards.
For the Council, he proposes three steps. States should agree on narrow bans first, then build evaluation and verification systems so they can check each other’s commitments.
They should also set common global standards for testing AI models, with a notification system for serious AI incidents.
“No leader, no company, and no nation can manage this alone,” he says.

articles.title: Microsoft refreshes its smaller Surface Pro and Laptop with Qualcomm’s X2 Plus
articles.text:
Microsoft is refreshing its Surface Pro 12-inch and Surface Laptop 13-inch devices with Qualcomm’s latest Snapdragon X2 Plus chips. The smaller Surface devices retain the same design and hardware features from last year, with faster and more capable chips inside and higher price tags (thanks RAMageddon!).
Microsoft refreshes its smaller Surface Pro and Laptop with Qualcomm’s X2 Plus
The Surface Pro 12-inch and Surface Laptop 13-inch both have better battery life and performance, but higher price tags.
While the 12-inch Surface Pro started at $799.99 last year, it’s debuting on October 13th at a starting price of $1,149.99. Likewise, the 13-inch Surface Laptop was originally priced at $899.99, but it’s up to $1,199.99 this time around. There’s no base 8GB model this time, causing some of the price increase, as both devices launch with a minimum of 16GB of RAM and can be configured up to 24GB.
Pricing aside, Microsoft is promising that the six-core Snapdragon X2 Plus chips will deliver up to 18 percent more efficient battery performance, more than 60 percent faster graphics performance, and up to 95 percent faster local AI inferencing on the built-in NPU.
That’s a lot of percentages, but what it equates to on these devices is better battery life and improved performance. On the Surface Pro 12-inch Second Edition, as Microsoft calls it, that means an extra hour of web browsing (up to 13 hours in total), and on the Surface Laptop 13-inch Second Edition it’s two extra hours of web browsing usage (up to 18 hours in total).
Microsoft is using similar displays on these models as last year, so the Surface Pro 12-inch has a 2196 x 1464 (220 PPI) LCD display that runs at up to 90Hz. The Surface Laptop 13-inch still ships with a 1920 x 1280 (178 PPI) display that only runs at 60Hz. Both displays have been upgraded from 400 nits of brightness to 500 nits, though.
Port selection remains the same, too. Both devices include two USB-C 3.2 ports, and the Surface Laptop 13-inch also has a USB-A 3.2 port and a 3.5mm headphone jack. Both also support Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 5.4 connectivity.
I’m surprised that Microsoft hasn’t upgraded at least one of these smaller Surface devices with a haptic trackpad, particularly because Windows 11 now adds subtle haptic nudges, and the Surface Laptop Ultra ships with haptic feedback. Microsoft is launching a second edition of its Surface Mouse with integrated haptics, and you can read all about that here.
Microsoft is also bringing back the black color option for both of these smaller Surface devices, with platinum silver or violet colors available too. Both devices will also be sold to commercial customers, and the Surface Pro 12-inch will be available in an optional 5G configuration.

articles.title: YouTube releases new AI features for creators within its Studio app | TechCrunch
articles.text:
At its Made On YouTube annual event, YouTube announced new tools for YouTube Studio, the app creators use to manage their channels, aimed at helping them analyze their videos and grow their audiences. The updates include expanding Ask Studio, its AI-powered Q&A feature, to iOS and Android, as well as new features that provide feedback on drafts and create dynamic thumbnails.
The draft-feedback feature uses AI to look at a creator’s unpublished video and provide suggestions about pacing, structure, and storytelling. YouTube is also debuting a new research feed in the Studio app that shows creators what kind of content is working on the platform, so they can apply their own take on it.
Creators are typically picky about the preview images and titles they use for their videos. The Studio app will now let them generate thumbnails and titles based on a video’s content and matched to their style. Creators can also use a new dynamic thumbnail feature to generate three options and show each one to a different segment of their audience.
YouTube said creators have used its A/B testing feature to run more than 40 million tests on titles and thumbnails. Soon, the company said, users will be able to test up to three video cuts to see which opening hook works best. Later this year, YouTube Studio will also automatically monitor thumbnail performance and change one proactively if it doesn’t perform well.
YouTube also said it’s updating its analytics to go beyond raw numbers, explaining why videos perform the way they do and providing advice about how to make content more engaging.
Besides the Studio app revamp, YouTube also introduced other tools for creators, including conversational editing in Shorts and the YouTube Create app.

articles.title: Yoshua Bengio urges UN Security Council to license frontier AI like nuclear power
articles.text:
Yoshua Bengio is calling on the UN Security Council to license frontier AI in areas like medicine, aviation, and nuclear energy.
Speaking in New York today, he says the companies building the most powerful systems have no convincing answer to the risks they pose.
Bengio, who co-chairs the UN’s scientific panel on AI, is opening a meeting convened by France. According to a Security Council Report, it is the Council’s first meeting focused specifically on the safety risks of increasingly capable AI.
He points to this summer’s incidents, in which AI agents escaped their containment, launched coordinated cyberattacks, and changed their answers to hide the fact that they had cheated.
“They took actions that would be crimes if committed by a human,” Bengio says.
Many people suspect the companies’ warnings are a marketing stunt, he acknowledges. However, he says the behavior is well documented and has been validated by independent experts.
“The companies building the most powerful AI systems admit their products pose catastrophic risks, yet offer no convincing technical solutions,” he says.
He also rejects the labs’ argument that competition leaves them no choice.
“The race is not a law of nature. It is the product of choices, choices made by the companies themselves. They’ve told us they would slow down if they could. They can,” Bengio says.
Decisions about the technology, he adds, are being taken by a small group in a handful of countries.
“Decisions that affect us all should be made by us all,” he says.
Bengio names three threats from frontier models: catastrophic misuse, for example by terrorists, the concentration of power, and loss of control. No company or country, he argues, should develop an AI system that could cause large-scale harm.
To that end, he wants frontier AI to be licensed like other critical technologies, with the required liability insurance. Companies should also monitor and report all security incidents, he says.
“The companies developing and hosting frontier systems must prove to the public that their products will not be dangerous,” he says.
Bengio closes by describing humanity’s situation as a car speeding blindly into dense fog.
“Beside me in that car are my children and my grandson. I worry about them,” he says.

articles.title: YouTube’s new ‘Shorts series’ feature brings episodic viewing to Shorts | TechCrunch
articles.text:
As microdrama apps gain traction, YouTube is clearly betting that episodic short-form storytelling will stick around. And that the format belongs on Shorts.
At its Made On YouTube event on Wednesday, the company announced “Shorts series,” a new tool that lets creators organize their Shorts into TV-style seasons and episodes. The feature brings a more traditional episodic structure to YouTube Shorts, complete with custom thumbnails and playback.
With Shorts series, viewers can watch a selection of Shorts as a continuous story rather than simply scrolling from one stand-alone clip to the next. The series will live on a creator’s YouTube channel.
The feature is rolling out to creators in the YouTube Partner Program across web, mobile, and connected TVs.
The move comes as no surprise, given that YouTubers have already been experimenting with microdramas and, increasingly, they’re considering it a serious business venture.
For instance, internet personality Hannah Stocking has crossed into vertical drama, starring in the musical microdrama “Playback,” which premiered on Holywater’s My Drama platform. Then there’s Joshua Ovenshire (The Jovenshire), a longtime YouTube creator who has moved away from traditional YouTube videos. He now works as an executive producer, making shows for vertical platform ReelShort, including a “Love Island”-inspired series called “Secrets and Soulmates.”
The format has even become popular enough to attract recognizable Hollywood names, with celebrities including James Franco, Issa Rae, and Jesse Tyler Ferguson getting involved.
YouTube’s new feature also puts the platform more directly into competition with a growing collection of microdrama apps. TikTok recently launched PineDrama, its own microdrama app, while others such as ReelShort and DramaBox have also grown in popularity.
For YouTube, Shorts series could be a way to keep viewers engaged without sending them off to other platforms for episodic vertical storytelling. Instead, they’re providing a way to access it all directly on YouTube.
The company adds that Shorts series builds on “Creator Shows,” which it announced at its annual upfront event last year. This gave select creators the tools to organize their content into a viewing experience designed for TV. Creators, including Michelle Khare and Rhett & Link, used the tools to structure their content into seasons and episodes, making it easier for viewers to binge on the big screen.
Other Made On YouTube announcements are also designed to help creators grow and engage audiences. This includes “Live Showdowns,” which let creators pair up for interactive team challenges; expanded video A/B testing to compare different cuts or opening hooks; “Dynamic Thumbnails” to allow YouTubers to select the most engaging option from up to three creator-provided thumbnails for different audiences; new shopping features; and more.

articles.title: Microsoft’s new Surface Mouse has haptic feedback and a customizable action button
articles.text:
Microsoft is launching a second generation of its Surface Mouse next month that includes haptic feedback support. The Surface Mouse also has a customizable action button for the first time, which is primarily designed for quick access to Copilot (of course), but can be configured to work with other shortcuts from the Surface app.
Microsoft’s new Surface Mouse has haptic feedback and a customizable action button
The $79.99 Surface Mouse will start shipping on October 13th.
“Its haptic feedback adds a small, purposeful physical response to the moment you usually only see on a screen: a click registering, a window snapping into place or an object aligning just right,” says Brett Ostrum, corporate vice president of Surface Devices. “It is subtle by design, but noticeable within seconds — and hard to give up once you have it.”
The haptic feedback works with things like clicks, drags, and alignment throughout Windows 11, but the tactile feedback also triggers in apps like PowerPoint, Affinity, Concepts, and Filmora. Microsoft added support for haptic feedback in Windows 11 earlier this year, and so far it’s mainly Microsoft and Logitech that are supporting it with dedicated hardware. Logitech’s MX Master 4 has haptic feedback, and its Pro X2 Superstrike (and today’s new X3) includes a haptic-based clicks system that doesn’t support the Windows 11 haptic feedback. The upcoming Surface Laptop Ultra also has a haptic trackpad.
After originally launching the Surface Mouse in 2016 and not updating it since, Microsoft has now redesigned it to be more comfortable for all-day use, with a soft-touch material at the top. Thanks to Bluetooth 6.0 support, you can now also pair it with up to three devices.
The new Surface Mouse will be available on October 13th, the same day Microsoft launches its refreshed Surface Pro 12-inch and Surface Laptop 13-inch devices. It will be priced at $79.99, and available in black and platinum color options.

articles.title: Sam Altman tells UN Security Council OpenAI will slow down
articles.text:
Sam Altman is calling for national and international standards for frontier AI. Speaking at the UN Security Council in New York today, the OpenAI chief executive says no level of catastrophic risk from AI is acceptable.
Altman is the second briefer at the meeting, which France convened. According to the Security Council Report, it is the Council’s first meeting focused specifically on the safety risks of increasingly capable AI.
It comes two months after OpenAI’s own agents broke into Hugging Face during an internal test.
“We’ve been talking about artificial intelligence for years, but it feels different in recent weeks and months,” Altman says.
He says he largely agrees with Yoshua Bengio, who spoke before him. However, he sees two main dangers rather than three: losing control of the future to AI, and AI concentrating power in too few hands. Being in a competitive race, he adds, is no reason to make rash decisions.
“We have unilaterally slowed down in the past. We will do so in the future,” he says.
No level of catastrophic risk is acceptable, Altman argues, whether people put it at 10% or 0.1%. Companies should not train models unless they can make a strong case that those models will stay under human control.
“No one person or company or country should be able to use the most powerful AI models to impose their worldview on everyone else,” he tells the Council.
Altman also points to OpenAI’s claim this month that one of its models solved the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem, a result that has not yet been independently verified.
“If AI is to be democratic, the most important decisions cannot be made by labs in San Francisco alone,” Altman says.
His proposals follow a standards proposal OpenAI published on Tuesday. He wants common standards for testing capabilities, assessing risks and keeping human oversight, so that countries can compare evidence and verify compliance.
He also calls for rapid incident reporting and secure channels among governments, infrastructure operators, and technical experts.
The standards, he says, should not lock in incumbents and should support both open and closed model developers.
“AI can either be more like a new renaissance of creativity and discovery, or more like a new industrial revolution of upheaval and disarray,” he says.
“We might be the builders, one of the builders of this technology, but we are not the heroes of the story,” Altman adds.

articles.title: YouTube adds new creator tools like video A/B testing, dynamic thumbnails, and live dubbing | TechCrunch
articles.text:
In a bid to help creators reach more people, YouTube on Wednesday unveiled a slew of new tools, many of which use AI to try out different tactics on videos to find what makes them perform best.
The new Ask Studio feature allows creators to share draft videos with AI to get personalized feedback based on their previous content and user comments. The feature will propose alternative titles and thumbnail options, analyze the creator’s channel analytics to explain the performance of their videos, and offer advice for improving metrics. Ask Studio is expanding to YouTube’s mobile apps, too.
YouTube already allows creators to A/B test titles and thumbnails, and from 2027, this feature will let creators upload and test three different cuts for Shorts. There’s also a Dynamic Thumbnails feature, with which creators can upload multiple thumbnails and leave it to YouTube to determine which thumbnail to show viewers that is most likely to spark their interest.
Creators can also apply these tools to their existing catalog. If a creator allows it, Ask Studio will be able to autonomously monitor thumbnail performance and create tests to refine older videos.
On the shopping front, YouTube will now use AI to auto-tag products, which it says will help creators earn money through affiliate programs. The company is also expanding its Amazon affiliate program beyond the U.S.
Some creators are understandably skeptical of using AI to support their content, worrying that just one AI-generated mistake could harm their credibility. For such features to succeed, they will need to be accurate enough to assuage creators’ concerns.
The platform is also giving creators new ways to go live. Early next year, YouTube will pilot auto-dubbing on live videos to translate creators’ speech into other languages in real time. The company is also launching a “live showdown” feature, which lets creators co-host streams together, and even get paired with other creators currently streaming through “live creator matchmaking.”
“Co-hosts can kick off friendly head-to-head matchups, where viewers send chats, gifts, and Super Chats to push their creator’s score forward on-screen in real time,” YouTube Live product manager Barbara MacDonald wrote in a blog post.
Hopefully these impromptu collaborations with strangers won’t turn into a hotbed of bad behavior.
YouTube also shared data that provides insight into how people are using the platform. More people continue to watch YouTube on household TVs, and more than half of the top 100 YouTube creators have “living room” as their most watched interface.
YouTube’s data also confirms what we know about the growth of the microdrama industry: In the first half of 2026, microdramas on YouTube surpassed 6.5 billion views, and their watch time rose 50% year-over-year. People even seem to be watching these episodic, vertical video series on the big screen, with views of microdrama content on TVs increasing 90% year-over-year.

articles.title: Meta’s AI agent is a cute little guy who’s great at spending my money
articles.text:
Modern life comes with an unending, auto-populating to-do list.
Meta’s AI agent is a cute little guy who’s great at spending my money
Muse did a decent job with my to-do list, but boy is it handy with a credit card.
Meta’s AI agent is a cute little guy who’s great at spending my money
Muse did a decent job with my to-do list, but boy is it handy with a credit card.
It never ceases to amaze me how I can be doing nothing at all, minding my own business, and suddenly something needs to be taken care of. You’re telling me a tree branch fell in the backyard and now I have to figure out what to do with it? The tree just assigned me homework? Oh, our trash collection company canceled our account out of nowhere and now I have to send email about it? Repeatedly? Totally unfair.
These are the things that we’ve been told for years that AI will help us with. We’ll all have a smart virtual assistant to triage and handle the tedious tasks we’d rather not face. If you believe Meta, that future is available right now in the form of Muse, its AI agent for the masses. I put it to the test doing exactly what it’s advertised to do: taking care of tedious crap I’ve been putting off for ages. And it worked better than I expected — especially when there was a credit card transaction to be made.
It was dizzying watching Marley spin up virtual browser windows chasing down my requests
Marley — one of the suggested names you can give Muse’s avatar — had been pinging me all of last week. It wanted me to know all the ways it could be useful; I was too busy to engage with it. But I sat down with it this week and set it to work on a task. And while it worked on that task, I gave it another. Then another. The thing about AI agents is that they’re most useful when you use them in parallel with each other. Or that’s the theory I was working on. In reality, it was dizzying watching Marley spin up virtual browser windows chasing down my requests. I went with a generically cute snowman-meets-puppy avatar that Meta suggested at setup, and Marley tapped cheerfully on a keyboard as it worked its way through my commands.
In the span of a morning, I gave it the following tasks to help me out with. None of them were critical; mostly they were the kinds of pebble-in-your-shoe annoyances I’d put off for weeks, months, or maybe years. Here’s how it went.
Task: Follow up with the landscaper working on a bid for our backyard renovation
Effort rating: Extremely low
Time I have been putting it off: Two weeks
Was Marley able to complete it? Yes
I asked Marley to help me nudge the person I’ve been emailing at a local landscaping company. I’m expecting them to price out some yard renovations for us, so Marley requested access to my Gmail to check on the status of that project. It confirmed that more time had passed than the landscaper initially estimated the bid would take, and drafted a rather snippy but wordy email. “Make it shorter,” I said. To be clear: As a rule, I do not use AI writing tools. Definitely not in my work, and not even for email. What’s the point? Just don’t send email if you’re going to have a robot write it. In fact, I think we should abolish email. Anyway, I broke my own rule for testing purposes; hitting send on that message made me cringe.
Task: Buy a replacement steam wand assembly for my espresso machine
Effort rating: Low
Time I have been putting it off: [redacted] years
Was Marley able to complete it? Mostly
My Breville Barista Express has held up spectacularly for six years and counting, but it isn’t immune from user error. I took the steam wand apart to clean it a few years back and tore the little silicone washer that goes inside of it. Instead of ordering a new one, I just shoved it back into place and screwed the thing back together. It works okay, but every few months when I’m cleaning the machine it nags at my conscience. It’s probably why the hot water dispenser drips sometimes when I run the steam, too. Ordering a new steam wand assembly costs like 7 bucks and is as difficult as entering my credit card number on Breville’s website. Naturally, I put it off for an unreasonable amount of time.
I opened up my chat with Marley and told it what I needed; it found the part and added it to a shopping cart. I had to finish up the order myself, but it’s done and the part will be here in five to seven business days.
Task: Downgrade my security system account to the cheaper one
Effort rating: Medium (requires a phone call)
Time I have been putting it off: A year? Two years???
Was Marley able to complete it? Not fully
I approved Marley to log into my account, which also required me to verify my email. While I was making the trip to my inbox I saw I had a follow-up to my follow-up with the landscaper. He was apologetic for the delay and I felt a little bad about the slightly abrupt tone of the email Marley sent. I wrote a friendlier reply the old-fashioned way.
With access to my account, Marley reported back what I already knew: You have to call the company to change your plan. Muse wasn’t able to make a phone call for me, though apparently that ability is in the works. This seems like the logical next frontier for these AI agents, and also a weird future to consider. I call the company and answer a few questions from their robot before I’m routed to a human. No doubt there’s a future soon where Marley talks to the security company’s robot before any human being enters the chat. Or more likely in the short term, a human in a call center talks to the other company’s robot before eventually getting to another human in a call center, which feels even weirder. But surely the end state is that my robot will just talk to their robot and they’ll do business without any intervention at all. Anyway, a nice guy answered and made the change to my account. I think he was real.
Task: Contact a junk removal company to get rid of a fallen tree branch in the backyard
Effort rating: Medium
Time I have been putting it off: A week
Was Marley able to complete it? Mostly
The tree branch is a real problem I need to deal with. It didn’t do any damage, but it’s big enough that it’ll either take an afternoon to hack apart and haul to the dump or requires a visit from a junk removal service. Marley was most useful here — it set off looking through listings for hauling services and highlighted a few in the area. It asked for my address, phone number, and a photo of the tree limb, and used that information to put together requests for quotes from a couple of companies using online form submissions. I got a text back from one company not long after, and confirmed a time the following day for tree limb removal. Very little was required on my part, and assuming the tree branch is gone by this time tomorrow, I’ll consider this mission accomplished for Muse.
Task: Shop for camping kitchen gear, either as a set or assembled piece by piece
Effort rating: Medium
Time I have been putting it off: A few days
Was Marley able to complete it? Yes
If our wallets were already defenseless in the era of one-click checkout, we’re so cooked when AI agent shopping truly arrives. I gave Marley some requirements for my outdoor cooking setup and it set out finding the necessary items. It made an attempt to access Amazon and was roundly blocked, complete with a spicy message about AI agents violating terms of service. Anyway, it found what I was looking for between OXO’s own website and Walmart.
While I was at it, I wanted to add a propane fire pit to the mix. Not for cooking — for ambience and marshmallows. I’d borrowed a couple of different kinds from friends, and after weighing the pros and cons of each with Muse I landed on a LavaBox and a handy carrying case. The grand total for my camp kitchen and burn-ban-safe fire pit: $500! I told Muse we’d have to pump the brakes and spread these purchases out over the winter. It obliged and helped me prioritize what would make sense to buy first and what was likely to go on sale toward the holidays.
In the meantime, I had Marley find and purchase some other espresso machine supplies. I had to connect my credit card via Stripe, but after I’d done that once it became dangerously easy to tell Marley “Go for it” and approve whatever it had just put in my shopping cart. I watched it fill in my address details in the virtual browser window and confirmation emails started filing into my inbox. Marley did a little shopping around to find slightly better prices, and I didn’t buy anything egregious — just some descaling powder and water filters. It also did the math to calculate whether powdered Dezcal would be a better value than the liquid stuff (way better, not surprisingly). But it is shockingly easy to spend money when a cute little guy is running around the internet with your credit card.
It is shockingly easy to spend money when a cute little guy is running around the internet with your credit card
There’s a danger in overcommitting yourself when you feel like these AI tools are speeding you up. In a few cases, Muse helped me get started by putting the details I needed in front of my face. I had the phone number for the home security company at hand, as well as the name of my current plan and the one I wanted to downgrade to. Getting that little speed bump out of the way was what I needed, I guess. But the dirty secret of productivity hacks is that doing more stuff often doesn’t feel like things are being removed from your plate; somehow it just invites more tasks.
If you’re willing to give a lot of information and trust to Meta — a massive caveat! — Muse can genuinely help you get things done. I’d been using it for all of 40 minutes and already given it my full name, address, credit card number, a photo of my backyard, and the credentials for my home security account login. Going great, I’d say! If AI decides to kill us all I just secured my spot at the front of the line. Meta of course says that all of these details are stored securely, Marley allegedly can’t even see them, etc., but still. Unsettling.
But I think the underlying question we need to ask ourselves as we enter the era of AI agents is what we do with the time we’re supposedly freeing up. Will we use it to take on more commitments? And then ultimately feel overwhelmed again when the to-do list keeps piling up? After a morning crossing items off my list with Marley, I didn’t spend the hours that followed doing anything consequential. In fact, I spent that time chatting with Marley, seeking reassurance about the direction of the yard project and brainstorming fall camping trips I probably won’t take. It’s a gorgeous day outside, the kind we really can’t take for granted in late September, and I wish I’d spent that time outdoors rather than inside talking to a robot, cute little guy or otherwise.
Photography by Allison Johnson / The Verge

articles.title: U.S.-China trade truce extended for two months, Bessent says, as Xi begins state visit
articles.text:
The U.S. and China have extended a truce to keep tariffs lower for longer and rare earths flowing, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Wednesday local time.
He was speaking on Fox News, as Chinese President Xi Jinping landed in Washington, D.C. for a state visit through Friday.
Xi and Trump agreed to a one-year trade truce at a meeting in South Korea last October. The deal, which was set to expire in November, will now be extended to Jan. 10, Bessent said. He added that Beijing needs to fulfill more deliverables.
Ahead of this week's summit, many had expected the truce would be extended by six months or longer.
Chinese state media did not immediately note Bessent's comments on the trade truce.
Footage streamed on China's state broadcaster showed U.S. President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump meeting Xi and First Lady of China Peng Liyuan at the foot of the Chinese leader's jet. The video did not show the U.S. and Chinese leaders shaking hands — it focused on Xi and his wife shaking hands with two children presenting them each with bouquets.
Bessent met with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York ahead of Xi's arrival in the U.S. The two sides discussed setting up an alert system for artificial intelligence incidents, according to Bessent.

articles.title: Flock, Axon dodge Senate hearing after invite from Chair Josh Hawley
articles.text:
The CEOs of major surveillance technology companies, including Flock Safety, did not attend a Senate hearing called by Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., to examine the proliferation of their products, which have come under scrutiny for potential breaches of privacy.
Hawley, chairman of the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism, invited Flock Safety CEO Garrett Langley, Axon Enterprise CEO Rick Smith, Motorola Solutions CEO Greg Brown and Verkada CEO Filip Kaliszan to testify at his Wednesday hearing to examine AI-powered surveillance cameras. None of the executives appeared before the committee.
"I invited all of them. Sen. Durbin and I did," Hawley said, referring to the committee's ranking member Sen. Dick Durbin, D-Ill. "I think we need to hear from them about what it is their networks do. I think we need to hear from them about their intentions, about their capabilities."
The hearing came as scrutiny intensifies around the companies, most notably Flock, which has an extensive network of AI-powered automated license plate readers. The nationwide network is accessible to customers, which include police departments, and has been credited with helping solve crimes.
But senators on the panel expressed widespread concern that the technology could lead to a dangerous surveillance network that infringes on people's rights. Five Indiana police officers were charged with crimes on Wednesday relating to misuse of the surveillance technology, and the committee heard from Lindsey Isaacs, who told the committee she was wrongly accused of being involved in a fatal crash due to a surveillance camera error.
"A customer in a Flock network, for example, just needs to buy a single camera and a subscription that I'm told costs about $3,000 annually, and in return for that they get access to a nationwide database of tens of thousands of cameras, about 120,000 in Flock's case and billions of images," Hawley said. "We need to have an honest conversation about where this is leading us as a country."
Hawley did not say during the hearing whether he would try to compel Flock and the other companies invited to appear before the committee. In an interview with reporters before the hearing, however, Hawley suggested the companies could be forced to testify.
"It's ridiculous," he said. "We have not subpoenaed them, though, and we should."
Congressional committees have subpoena power, meaning they can compel individuals to testify if they do not appear voluntarily.
Scrutiny of Flock and other surveillance providers was largely bipartisan at the hearing, as did disdain for the company leaders not appearing.
"For the Flock CEOs, obviously they're nervous about being on camera," Durbin said. "I sure wish they would have joined us today."
Flock, Axon and Motorola did not respond to requests for comment from CNBC.
A spokesperson for Verkada said that "Unfortunately, our CEO was unable to attend today's hearing." The company also denied having a national database.
"We are in communication with the Subcommittee and are providing information to assist Chairman Hawley and Ranking Member Durbin as they prepare for the hearing," the spokesperson said. "As we've explained to the Subcommittee, none of our customers can search a national Verkada network – because none exists. Our customers can only access the data in their own systems."
In a letter to Hawley dated Sep. 8, Flock's chief legal officer Dan Haley said the company recognizes "the importance of, and [is] committed to building upon, the significant, proactive steps we have taken over the last year to strengthen our ability to prevent and detect misuse of our technology."
Flock also said it would support "clear, sensible legislation governing how this technology is used. Durable legislation and legal standards are the foundation of the public trust on which our business depends."
Semafor reported Wednesday that Flock is considering selling itself.
— CNBC's Karen James Sloan contributed to this report.

articles.title: Stock futures are flat after soaring Treasury yields trigger a market sell-off: Live updates
articles.text:
Stock futures hovered near the flatline Wednesday night after surging yields in Treasurys sparked a sell-off in the market and traders anticipated rate hikes from the Federal Reserve.
S&P 500 futures were up 0.02%, while futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 6 points, or 0.01%. Nasdaq-100 futures gained 0.08%.
During the regular trading day, the Dow Industrials fell more than 350 points, or 0.7%, while the S&P 500 slid 0.8%. The Nasdaq Composite lost 1.1% and broke a four-day win streak.
The benchmark 10-year Treasury note yield, which is tied to rates on mortgages, surged to 5.135% for its highest level since July 2007. The yield on the 2-year note climbed to 4.947% for its highest since May 2024.
As yields surged, so did the market's anticipation of further rate hikes from central bank policymakers. Fed funds futures trading suggests a greater than 68% likelihood that the policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee lifts its key rate once more in October, according to the CME FedWatch tool. That compares to a roughly 49% probability just a week ago.
Higher yields tend to squeeze consumers' finances as they face higher borrowing costs at a time when they're already paying more in fuel costs.
Oil prices bounced Wednesday. International Brent crude futures rose about 3.9% to settle at $103.08 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate crude gained 1.8% to $92.16.
Readings from S&P Global's manufacturing and services purchasing managers' indexes suggested that U.S. businesses are continuing to boom. BMO Capital Markets said in a Wednesday note that even as the results were strong, "severe supply chain bottlenecks," as well as higher fuel and transport prices, can drive inflation.
"Overall, it was a much stronger-than-expected read on US business activity that implies ample latitude for both policy rates and Treasury yields to push higher in the near-term," said Vail Hartman, a U.S. rates strategist at BMO. "If anything, the data reinforces the risk of a renewed acceleration in demand-driven inflation even if supply-side inflation subsides."
Going into Thursday, traders will be watching weekly jobless claims for further details on the state of the economy. On the earnings front, they'll also look for quarterly results from Olive Garden parent Darden Restaurants in the morning and big-box retailer Costco Wholesale in the afternoon.

articles.title: Meta's standoff with Amazon over Muse could be a sign of things to come
articles.text:
Meta's rollout of its Muse AI personal agent has been a big hit with consumers and investors. The stock has jumped more than 20% in the two weeks since its introduction, and the app has shot up to the top of Apple's App Store, eclipsing ChatGPT.
Mark Zuckerberg took to the stage late Wednesday afternoon at the company's annual Connect conference for developers to relish in the excitement, and described the Muse AI agent as representing the "centerpiece" of his company's efforts to make the technology more easily available to the broader public instead of coders.
"In the coming years, I expect that Muse is going to grow into the personal superintelligence that billions of people around the world are going to use to accomplish their goals and improve their lives," Zuckerberg said.
But there are reasons for skepticism regarding Meta's latest effort to find a real and lasting niche in the consumer artificial intelligence market.
Meta is touting Muse's ability to book appointments and travel, fill out electronic forms for users, and monitor home security cameras. It can also shop on a user's behalf, searching for a specific product across various sites and marketplaces and linking to Shopify or Stripe for payment.
Amazon has said that's a no-go, blocking Muse from purchasing products on the e-commerce app, claiming that it would violate the company's terms of service. Whether it's other retailers taking similar steps out of concern that they're at risk of losing the direct relationship with customers, or it's consumers that don't trust the Facebook parent with sensitive data, experts say the social media giant has a long way to go to turn its early momentum in Muse into a winning product.
"People are going to be very wary," said Joseph Turow, a professor emeritus at the University of Pennsylvania and an expert on digital media and privacy. "Some people are going to dip their toes into it, and some people are going to accept it for particular companies that they trust."
Turow said there will be "early adopters," and then others will get "seduced into this," seeing that using this sort of personal agent can save them money by finding the best discounts.
Zuckerberg is pushing deeper into the agentic AI market at a fraught moment for the the AI industry and for Meta. Anthropic and OpenAI are calling for a slowdown in the pace of model development as fears intensify that advanced AI is spinning out of human control and, unless it gets reined in, could threaten humanity or at least amplify cybersecurity attacks.
Meta, meanwhile, agreed last month to pay up to $17 billion to settle a lawsuit brought by a host of states that alleged the company misrepresented the extent of child mental health harms caused by apps like Facebook and Instagram. The emergence of generative AI and chatbots has made the issue of online addiction even more pressing, as both OpenAI and Google have been sued by plaintiffs alleging their technology caused harm, including suicides.
'Fiercely guarding the customer relationship'
Amazon has made clear in the recent past that it won't let AI services stand between the company and its customers. It sued Perplexity in November, alleging the startup took steps to "conceal" its AI agents so they could continue to scrape the retailer's website without its approval. Amazon has also blocked agentic tools from OpenAI and Google.
Amazon's "whole model is fiercely guarding the customer relationship," said Matthew Hassett, CEO of smart alarm clock company Loftie, which sells on Amazon, and of AI-focused ecommerce startup Deliberate. "'Respect service provider decisions' is the polite version of 'not on our shelf.'"
Hassett was quoting Amazon, which said in a statement that "third-party applications that offer to make purchases on behalf of customers from other businesses should operate openly and respect service provider decisions about whether or not to participate."
Meta declined to comment.
Max Willens, an analyst at Emarketer, said that as more consumers use AI agents like Muse, Amazon will get more protective of its role in the "consumer journey."
"For many years, Amazon was the place most U.S. consumers went first if they wanted to buy something online," Willens said "Today, those consumers are increasingly starting those shopper journeys with AI assistants."
While Amazon may not approve of Meta's Muse AI agent, other retailers appear more on board. Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang said during the Connect keynote that social media giant has enlisted Muse partners including Walmart, Best Buy, Gap, Sephora, Wayfair, and others, in a bid to help the AI agent "enable new shopping experiences."
"One of the great promises of ecommerce since the earliest days of the industry has been that it can save you money and time," Wang said. "Personal agents are going to continue delivering on that promise for a new generation of shoppers, and they're going to help them discover products they love and get great deals too."
Outside of commerce, Muse is raising concern that other industries could see Meta's new agent take over powerful functionality. Shares of financial services companies including Charles Schwab and LPL Financial Holdings tumbled on Tuesday, while travel sites Booking Holdings and Expedia plummeted on Wednesday.
For Meta, the early Muse momentum has reignited optimism on Wall Street, where the stock had been underperforming most of its megacap peers and the broader tech sector this year. With the post-Muse rally, the shares are now up 13% in 2026, just below the Nasdaq's 16% gain.
Analysts at Cantor who recommend buying Meta shares published a report on Tuesday with the headline, "Meta is racing while AI is pacing." They wrote that the business model isn't yet clear for a company that generates almost all of its revenue from digital ads, but the opportunity is apparent.
"We believe the unit economics of Muse are being subsidized in the early days, but we think META has several paths to a profitable freemium model," the analysts wrote.
Mizuho analysts, who also have the equivalent of a buy rating on the stock, said Meta Connect lands at just the right time for the company to link Muse with its AI narrative, particularly around wearables. While Meta never found a big market for its Quest-branded virtual reality glasses, it's seeing much higher adoption of its smart glasses, in partnership with Ray-Ban parent EssilorLuxottica
"We expect Connect to move the Muse story from app adoption to platform creation," the Mizuho analysts wrote on Tuesday. "The likely headline is Muse-on-glasses, combining Meta's rapidly growing AI agent with wearables and creating what we view as the clearest consumer AI use case yet."
— CNBC's Isabel O'Brien contributed to this report.
WATCH: Meta Connect 2026 happens Wednesday. Here's what to expect.

articles.title: People who 'flourish' in high-stakes meetings do 2 things before they walk in the room, says Harvard negotiation expert
articles.text:
Tonight, when President Donald Trump and President Xi Jinping greet each other at Joint Base Andrews ahead of their summit, the cameras will capture a handshake, a smile, maybe a joint statement.
What they won't capture is the weeks of preparation that made that handshake possible — the small but impactful choices made long before anyone walks into the room.
I've taught negotiation and behavioral economics at Harvard Business School for over a decade. You don't need to be a head-of-state to deal with high-stakes meetings. Whether it's a tense performance review, a make-or-break client pitch or a family conversation about money, the same principles apply.
The secret is all in the prep. Specifically, two kinds.
Stage the room like a director blocking a scene
Long before President Xi's plane touches down, someone will have decided where the two leaders would meet, who would host, and how the room would be arranged.
Research on negotiation has found that there is indeed a "home field advantage." When people negotiate in their own space, they often perform better than the visitors, in part because familiar turf breeds confidence.
And yet most of us give almost no thought to the physical organization of our own high-stakes meetings: where we sit, whether there's a table between us, a round shape versus a square one, and on and on.
Think of it the way a director thinks about blocking a scene. Choreography shapes what people are willing to say.
Stop prepping stilted talking points—try this instead
When you are getting ready for an important meeting, my best advice is to focus less on what you will say and more on what you will ask. Instead of prepping talking points, prep a learning agenda — a little list of things you want to find out from your counterpart.
You want to know four key things:
- What has changed for them since you last spoke?
- What pressure are they under?
- What does a good outcome look like from their side of the table?
- What is more versus less important to them?
This unlocks more than you might think at first glance, for several reasons. There's of course the obvious benefit that questions elicit information, and information is king. But, if you're anything like me and are prone to nervous oversharing, being ready with these questions gives your anxious energy somewhere useful to go.
In competitive and high-stakes rooms, anything you say can and will be used against you, and a well-timed question is a much safer place to put that energy than a blurted out tangent. Yes, I speak from experience here.
And then there is perhaps the most underappreciated aspect of this preparation. Decades of research on self-disclosure and trust show that asking questions causes others to like and trust you — which in turn causes them to reveal even more, creating a virtuous cycle.
The learning agenda shouldn't be all, or even mostly, business. The best agendas include a few non-serious questions too, maybe even a joke.
If you do this prep, something magical happens. You're freed up to just listen. To be present, to follow up on what you're hearing, and to respond like a real person instead of reciting a script. Paradoxically, the more you prepare, the more natural you're able to be.
None of this guarantees a good outcome in the moment, or in your next hard conversation. But it improves the odds, because what distinguishes those who flourish from those who flounder in these rooms is often in the preparation nobody sees.
Leslie John is the author of "Revealing: The Underrated Power of Oversharing" and James E. Burke Professor of Business Administration and Unit Head, Negotiations Organizations, and Markets Unit, Harvard Business School.

articles.title: Markets are rapidly coming around to the reality that the Fed has a lot more work to do
articles.text: The financial markets may be coming to the realization that the Federal Reserve is on the precipice of a full-blown hiking cycle and not merely an adjustment or tweak to its monetary policy. The 10-year Treasury note yield surged the most since April 2025 on Wednesday to 5.116%, its highest since 2007. The 2-year Treasury note yield , which is most sensitive to Fed policy, jumped to its highest since 2024. Last week, the Fed raised rates for the first time since 2023 and signaled that one more was coming this year before it is done. Expectations on Fed rate hikes are divided on Wall Street: hawkish views cap it at three quarter-point hikes to undo 2025's cuts, while dovish economists believe the rate hikes may already be over. Both perspectives reflect expectations of targeted policy recalibration rather than an aggressive tightening cycle. History shows that isolated tweaks are rare. Back in March 1997, the Fed delivered a single quarter-point hike and stopped there because annual inflation fell from 3% to 2.2% within three months. Beyond that, hiking cycles have usually been much larger. In the modern era, the smallest hiking cycle was 137 basis points (1986-87), the median 313 basis points and the average 478 basis points, according to Deutsche Bank Global Head of Macro and Thematic Research Jim Reid. (1 basis point equals 0.01%.) Reid also points to a New York Fed study showing that markets almost always underestimate the total extent of Fed rate increases. Yields rose by double digits Wednesday across the curve due to the potential that another rate hike may come as soon as October. A hot PMI report from S & P Global that showed business growth surging to its fastest level in almost five years and comments from Fed Governor Michael Barr that "further policy adjustments are likely" increase the odds of an October hike from about 50% to 70%. US2Y YTD mountain 2-year Treasury yield, YTD But yields aren't just spiking over a potential move next meeting, bond investors are worried about how many more hikes lie ahead. Rate hikes can't easily fix supply-side issues like the prolonged energy shock taking place right now. And Big Tech keeps spending heavily on AI regardless of borrowing costs, which means the Fed might have to act more aggressively to tamp down inflation expectations.

articles.title: A rare Microsoft bear warms up to the stock. Here's what changed their mind
articles.text: One of the few Microsoft bears on Wall Street has changed their tune, betting the tech giant's summer rebound has more runway ahead. Stifel upgraded Microsoft to buy from hold and raised its price target to $575 from $530, representing more than 15% upside from Tuesday's close. The analysts have grown more confident in Microsoft's growth trajectory, especially at its all-important Azure cloud unit, and less worried about pressure on the company's margins. With Stifel joining the bulls, there are only two remaining Wall Street firms with holds on Microsoft and no sell recommendations, according to FactSet data; there are 57 buy or buy-equivalent ratings. Shares of Microsoft are up fractionally Wednesday, bucking the broader market declines and weakness in cloud-computing peers Amazon , Google and Oracle . Microsoft "clearly turned the corner post the June quarter print," Stifel analysts wrote to clients in a note dated Tuesday. That's also the quarter that positively shifted Jim Cramer's view of the stock following months of disappointment in the enterprise software giant. MSFT 1Y mountain Microsoft's one-year stock performance. Shares came into that earnings release on July 28 down roughly 19% year to date. The stock was held back by a cocktail of concerns: that AI would upend the software industry, giving rise to the "SaaSpocalypse" narrative; that its much-maligned Copilot was falling behind rival AI tools; and that astronomical spending on AI data centers lacked a clear payoff. Then Microsoft delivered impressive results for both Azure and Copilot, and showed relative discipline on AI infrastructure spending, leaving its capital expenditure outlook for calendar year 2026 unchanged. Microsoft shares surged 15.5% in following the session and kept climbing from there, before topping out on Aug. 28 at $513.53. The stock has drifted about 2.5% lower over the past few weeks. Still, as of Wednesday, Microsoft remains up over 3% this year, a remarkable return to the green. Shares are about 8% below last October's all-time closing high. "We are increasingly comfortable with the company's ability to sustain mid/upper teens revenue growth," Stifel wrote, pointing to compelling drivers across both its cloud and enterprise software businesses. Microsoft's profitability is also stabilizing, analysts said, and its cash flow performance suggests less need for raising debt or equity than some hyperscaler peers. After what Stifel called a few "lackluster quarters," Azure is going in the right direction again and more data center capacity is coming online to meet demand. Azure's revenue growth rate accelerated to 43% on a constant-currency basis in its most recent quarter — compared with 39% and 38% in the March and December periods. The June quarter easily surpassed the FactSet consensus of of 40.4%. "Looking forward, we expect Azure upside to more closely mirror June results (200-300 bps of upside)," analysts wrote. "Microsoft appears to be hitting a more sustained efficiency cadence across the stack from silicon, models and software within Azure operations, likely freeing up additional capacity that can be effectively monetized in real-time by 3rd party apps/customers." Microsoft is also benefiting from the uptick in OpenAI's business, Stifel noted. Microsoft, which has invested billions in OpenAI over the years, receives a 20% revenue share from OpenAI, and Azure is the ChatGPT creator's primary cloud provider. Stifel is also upbeat on Copilot's future. Paid seats topped 30 million in Microsoft's June quarter, up 10 million from the prior quarter. Stifel expects Copilot and other AI tools to help sustain healthy average revenue per user gains for the Microsoft 365 software subscription business in years to come. One of the reasons Stifel had previously been more downbeat on Microsoft was expected pressure on profitability, but analysts conceded that "our expectations were too negative." Microsoft eliminating its own revenue shares to OpenAI helps change the calculus, as do efficiency gains at Azure. Though Stifel is the lone firm to upgrade Microsoft this week, it is the fourth to raise its price target, reflecting the stock's improved standing from just a few months earlier. Oppenheimer went to $570 from $510 on Tuesday. A day earlier, Cantor Fitzgerald went to $608 from $522 . Like Stifel, Cantor and Oppenheimer analysts were both enthused with Azure's momentum and kept their buy-equivalent ratings on Microsoft. Also on Monday, Rothschild & Co. Redburn lifted its price target to $440 from $400, but the firm stayed in the skeptic camp, reiterating its rare hold rating. Analysts cited concerns over the underlying economics of the AI infrastructure buildout. Despite a growing debate this month on whether to slow the development of AI models, there's been little sign that investment into compute infrastructure is moderating. On Wednesday, Microsoft said it will invest over $10 billion across the Middle East by 2030 to expand its data center presence. Bottom line The Club's stance on Microsoft is clear. "We're just going to keep holding [the stock]," said portfolio director Jeff Marks on Wednesday's Morning Meeting . Jeff agreed with Stifel that the most recent quarter signaled a turning point for Azure and Copilot. "Plus, this is one of the few hyperscalers that is living within their means. And what I mean by that is that they're still free cash flow positive," said Jeff. He also noted that Microsoft raising its dividend last week is another encouraging sign for Microsoft's future cash flows. The Club raised its Microsoft price target to $550 from $500 on Sept. 3, signaling our confidence in the company's resurgence and the market's improved attitudes toward software. But we kept our hold-equivalent 2 rating, preferring to wait for a better chance to buy after the stock's rally since reporting in July. (Jim Cramer's Charitable Trust is long MSFT and CRM.
